title: [Editor] HTTP Monitor header masking and Export use RedactionPolicy.Default, and Export writes captured bodies unredacted
body:
## Summary
The Monitor window masks headers and exports captures with the static RedactionPolicy.Default rather than the active MonitorInterceptor.RedactionPolicy. Export also writes captured request and response bodies in clear, as text and as base64. A developer who turns off capture redaction and relies on export masking leaks custom credential headers and body secrets into exported files.

## Location
- `Editor/Monitor/HttpMonitorWindow.Export.cs:133`

## Problem
HttpMonitorWindow.Export.cs:96 (RedactionPolicy.Default.RedactUrl), 131-135 (comment 'Always mask confidential headers in exports to prevent credential leakage when files are shared', implemented with RedactionPolicy.Default.IsSensitiveHeader) and HttpMonitorWindow.Panels.cs:453 (display mask) hard-code the default header list; none reads MonitorInterceptor.RedactionPolicy (MonitorInterceptor.cs:144). Export.cs:105-116 and 146-161 write request and response bodies as 'text' and 'base64' with no redaction, while the sibling Testing module redacts JSON and form bodies (RecordReplayTransport.Redaction.cs:81-95). With capture-time redaction on (the default), the 'Mask Confidential Headers' toggle (Panels.cs:26-34, TurboHttpSettings.cs:78-82) has no visible effect because values are already '[REDACTED]'.

**Failure scenario.** A developer turns 'Redact Captured Secrets' off to get replayable captures and relies on the export masking: a custom credential header (Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key, X-Functions-Key, a game session header) is exported in clear because it is not in the default list and there is no way to extend the list Export uses; an OAuth token response body is exported with access_token and refresh_token intact, twice.

## Suggested fix
Use one policy instance for capture, display and export (the active policy, or active policy united with Default for export), and apply the body redaction that #117 plans to the export path. Remove or repurpose the redundant mask toggle.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Monitor display and Export use the same redaction policy instance as capture (the active policy, with Default entries always included for export)
- [ ] Custom sensitive headers added to the active policy are masked in the window and in exported files
- [ ] Exported bodies pass through the body redaction defined for #117, or are omitted unless the user explicitly opts in
- [ ] The redundant mask toggle is removed or given a defined purpose
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Editor/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `util-design-05` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/util.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: code-smell.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Editor/Monitor/HttpMonitorWindow.Export.cs:96 and 131-135 and Panels.cs:451-459 use the static RedactionPolicy.Default, never MonitorInterceptor.RedactionPolicy; Export.cs:105-116,146-161 write captured bodies as text and base64 with no redaction. The header gap matters only when capture-time redaction is off or was overwritten (util-design-04): with a custom policy active, values are already [REDACTED] at capture. The body gap is unconditional (the Monitor has no body redaction at all). Open #117 (v1.1) tracks exactly this: 'One policy object drives every redaction site' plus an optional body redaction delegate consumed by the Monitor.

Related: #92, #117.

title: [Editor] HttpMonitorWindow.DrawDetailsPanel returns between BeginVertical and EndVertical when nothing is selected
body:
## Summary
DrawDetailsPanel returns early without a selection, after BeginVertical was called and before EndVertical. In the initial window state every layout and repaint ends with an unbalanced GUI group. Whether Unity 2021.3 logs a GUI error needs the Editor to confirm.

## Location
- `Editor/Monitor/HttpMonitorWindow.Panels.cs:183`

## Problem
HttpMonitorWindow.Panels.cs:178-184 calls EditorGUILayout.BeginVertical(), draws a HelpBox and returns when _selectedEvent == null; the matching EndVertical is at 227. OnGUI (HttpMonitorWindow.cs:140-151) then calls EndHorizontal, which closes the vertical group instead and leaves the horizontal group open for the rest of the event. The same file also rebuilds the whole 'Raw' text from both bodies (up to 5 MB each) on every OnGUI event (336-387).

**Failure scenario.** With no request selected (the initial state of the window) every Layout/Repaint ends with an unbalanced layout group; adding any control after the details panel in OnGUI would be laid out inside the wrong group. Whether Unity 2021.3 logs a GUI error here needs the Editor to confirm.

## Suggested fix
Use if/else (or try/finally) so EndVertical always runs; cache the Raw tab text per selected event.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] DrawDetailsPanel calls EndVertical on every path (if/else or try/finally)
- [ ] The Raw tab text is cached per selected event instead of rebuilt per OnGUI event
- [ ] Opening the window with nothing selected logs no GUI layout errors in Unity 2021.3 (checked in the Editor and recorded)
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Editor/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context

title: [Editor] HTTP Monitor details panel re-decodes full captured bodies and rebuilds the Raw view on every OnGUI event
body:
## Summary
The details panel decodes request and response bodies and rebuilds the raw view each OnGUI event. For a 5 MB JSON response this allocates about 10 MB (Response tab) to 30 MB (Raw tab) per event, and OnGUI runs on every mouse move and on the 10 Hz repaint during capture. This causes GC spikes and a sluggish editor with large captures.

## Location
- `Editor/Monitor/HttpMonitorWindow.Panels.cs:336`

## Problem
DrawResponseTab/DrawRequestTab pass `_selectedEvent.GetResponseBodyAsString()` / `GetRequestBodyAsString()` straight to EditorGUILayout.TextArea (HttpMonitorWindow.Panels.cs:251, 285) and DrawRawTab builds a StringBuilder with both bodies plus headers and calls ToString() (336-387) on each call. GetBodyAsString decodes the whole ReadOnlyMemory<byte> with UTF8.GetString and, when truncated, concatenates a suffix (a second full copy) (Runtime/Observability/HttpMonitorEvent.cs:207-233); nothing is cached per event or tab. OnGUI runs at least twice per repaint (Layout + Repaint) plus once per mouse/keyboard event, and captures are allowed up to MaxCaptureSizeBytes = 5 MB per body (budget/4 = 8 MB; MonitorInterceptor.cs:23, 591-603). DrawHeaders/AppendRawHeaders also allocate and sort a list per call (438-449) and DrawRequestRow allocates 3-4 strings per visible row per event (150, 158, 165).

**Failure scenario.** Select a captured 5 MB JSON response and open the Response or Raw tab: each OnGUI event allocates a 10 MB UTF-16 string (Response) or ~30 MB (Raw: body string, StringBuilder growth, ToString); moving the mouse over the window or the 10 Hz repaint while requests are being captured produces hundreds of MB/s of LOH garbage and the Editor stutters. IMGUI text rendering is also limited to roughly 16k characters per control, so most of that text is never shown.

## Suggested fix
Cache the decoded request/response/raw strings per selected event (invalidate on selection or mask toggle), cap the displayed text (first N KB with a 'copy full body' / export action), and build row labels once when the filtered cache is rebuilt.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Decoded request, response and raw strings are cached per selected event and invalidated on selection change or mask toggle
- [ ] Displayed text is capped (first N KB) with a copy-full-body or export action for the rest
- [ ] Row labels are built once when the filtered cache is rebuilt
- [ ] Repainting a selected 5 MB capture allocates no per-event body strings (measured allocation count per OnGUI event is zero after the first)
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Editor/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `util-runtime-04` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/util.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: performance.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. OnGUI redraws the details panel on every event (HttpMonitorWindow.cs:140-151; Panels.cs:186-204); DrawRequestTab/DrawResponseTab call GetRequestBodyAsString()/GetResponseBodyAsString() inline (Panels.cs:251,285) and DrawRawTab rebuilds a StringBuilder with both bodies and calls ToString() (336-386). GetBodyAsString decodes the whole captured memory with no cache and concatenates a suffix when truncated (HttpMonitorEvent.cs:207-233); captures may be up to 5 MB per body (MonitorInterceptor.cs:23,591-603). GetSortedHeaders allocates and sorts per call (Panels.cs:438-449). No caching field exists in the window. Editor-only cost with large captured bodies, so low rather than medium.

Related: [[R11-util-design-31]].

title: [Editor] HttpMonitorWindow and TurboHttpSettings are public with mutable static state that does not apply changes
body:
## Summary
The Editor tooling types are public with mutable static fields although nothing outside the Editor assembly and its tests needs them. Setting TurboHttpSettings.RedactCapturedSecrets from a project script does not reach the running MonitorInterceptor, which keeps RedactionPolicy.None until the next play-mode transition or Preferences edit. Users assume capture is redacted when it is not.

## Location
- `Editor/Monitor/HttpMonitorWindow.cs:22`

## Problem
HttpMonitorWindow is a public non-sealed partial class with 'public static bool DefaultMaskConfidentialHeaders { get; set; }' (HttpMonitorWindow.cs:16-22), written only by TurboHttpSettings.ApplyMonitorPreferences (TurboHttpSettings.cs:146). TurboHttpSettings is a public static class whose eight properties are thin EditorPrefs wrappers (39-115) that change stored preferences without applying them (only the settings GUI calls ApplyMonitorPreferences, 177-186). Editor/AssemblyInfo.cs already grants InternalsVisibleTo to TurboHTTP.Tests.Editor, and the build processors in the same assembly are internal.

**Failure scenario.** A project script sets TurboHttpSettings.RedactCapturedSecrets = true and assumes capture is redacted from that point; the running MonitorInterceptor keeps RedactionPolicy.None until the next play-mode transition or Preferences edit.

## Suggested fix
Make the window and settings internal, or make each public setter apply the change (call ApplyMonitorPreferences) and seal the window.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Window and settings types are internal, or each public setter applies its change through ApplyMonitorPreferences
- [ ] The window class is sealed
- [ ] Setting a preference from code takes effect on the running MonitorInterceptor immediately
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Editor/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context

Verification: Not independently verified: low-severity findings were not sent to a second reviewer. Re-trace it in the code before fixing.

title: [Editor] HttpMonitorWindow adds to EditorApplication.delayCall from the request-completing thread, which can lose callbacks and stop refresh
body:
## Summary
The window subscribes to EditorApplication.delayCall from whichever thread completes the request. delayCall is a plain static delegate field, so a cross-thread += can be overwritten by a concurrent main-thread update, losing this or another tool's callback. The flush never runs, the pending-refresh flag stays set and every later capture returns early, leaving the window permanently stale.

## Location
- `Editor/Monitor/HttpMonitorWindow.cs:84`

## Problem
MonitorInterceptor.PublishEvent invokes OnRequestCaptured on the capturing thread (MonitorInterceptor.cs:848-867), which is a thread-pool thread because the pipeline awaits with ConfigureAwait(false) (MonitorHandler.cs:74, ObservedResponseBodySource.cs:148). The window handler sets _pendingUiRefresh and executes `EditorApplication.delayCall += FlushCaptureOnMainThread` on that thread (HttpMonitorWindow.cs:77-85). `delayCall` is a public static field of delegate type (not a field-like event), so `+=` is an unsynchronised read-combine-write that races with the main thread's own `+=`/`-=` and with the editor's read-clear-invoke of the field. _pendingUiRefresh is cleared only in FlushCaptureOnMainThread and OnDisable (HttpMonitorWindow.cs:94, 74).

**Failure scenario.** Play Mode with the Monitor window open and requests completing on pool threads while the editor (or any other editor tool) touches delayCall on the main thread: (a) the background write is overwritten -> Flush never runs, _pendingUiRefresh stays 1, every later capture returns early at line 79-82 and the list stops updating until the window is closed and reopened; (b) the background write overwrites a main-thread update -> another tool's delayed callback is dropped or invoked twice.

## Suggested fix
Never touch EditorApplication delegates off the main thread: subscribe a main-thread pump once in OnEnable (EditorApplication.update polling the Interlocked flag) or capture the editor SynchronizationContext in OnEnable and Post to it from the callback.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] No EditorApplication delegate is touched off the main thread
- [ ] Refresh is driven by a main-thread pump (EditorApplication.update polling an Interlocked flag, or the editor SynchronizationContext captured in OnEnable)
- [ ] After captures arrive from pool threads concurrently with main-thread delayCall use, the window still refreshes
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Editor/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `util-runtime-03` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/util.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: concurrency.

Verification: Plausible: the code is as described; the outcome depends on runtime, device or peer behaviour that a static review cannot settle.

Verifier note: Code is as described: OnRequestCaptured sets _pendingUiRefresh and does EditorApplication.delayCall += FlushCaptureOnMainThread (HttpMonitorWindow.cs:77-85) on whatever thread MonitorInterceptor.PublishEvent runs (MonitorInterceptor.cs:848-867), which is a pool thread for real transports (MonitorHandler.cs:74; ObservedResponseBodySource.cs:148); the flag is cleared only in Flush and OnDisable (HttpMonitorWindow.cs:74,94), so a lost subscription leaves the list stale until the window is re-enabled. Whether the += can be lost depends on Unity's internal handling of the delayCall field and on a nanosecond interleaving with the editor loop, neither checkable here. Editor-only tool, no runtime impact.

title: [Editor] TurboHttpSettings overwrites MonitorInterceptor's static RedactionPolicy and capacity on every domain reload and play-mode transition
body:
## Summary
ApplyMonitorPreferences runs on domain reload and play-mode changes and assigns the public static MonitorInterceptor configuration from Editor preferences. A RedactionPolicy or capacity set by application code through the public API is silently replaced by Default or None. Custom sensitive headers then get captured and shown in clear.

## Location
- `Editor/Settings/TurboHttpSettings.cs:143`

## Problem
MonitorInterceptor.cs:139-148 documents a public setter for RedactionPolicy (custom policies via WithSensitiveHeaders, RedactionPolicy.cs:91-98) and public setters for HistoryCapacity, MaxCaptureSizeBytes, BinaryPreviewBytes, MaxTotalCaptureBytes, CaptureWithoutViewer, CaptureEnabled. TurboHttpSettings.cs:117-122 ([InitializeOnLoad] static constructor), 124-133 (playModeStateChanged EnteredPlayMode/EnteredEditMode) and 185 (any Preferences edit) call ApplyMonitorPreferences, which at 137-147 assigns all of those from EditorPrefs; line 143-145 can only produce RedactionPolicy.Default or RedactionPolicy.None. The Preferences UI has no field for extra sensitive headers. Tests/Editor/HttpMonitorRedactionSettingsTests.cs:41-58 asserts the Default/None assignment and has no case for a pre-existing custom policy. The auto-wired monitor exists only in the Editor (UHttpClient.cs:794), which is exactly where this overwrite runs.

**Failure scenario.** Game code sets MonitorInterceptor.RedactionPolicy = RedactionPolicy.Default.WithSensitiveHeaders("X-Session-Token") from a BeforeSceneLoad initializer or Awake. PlayModeStateChange.EnteredPlayMode then fires ApplyMonitorPreferences and the policy is Default again: X-Session-Token values are captured in clear, shown in the Monitor and written by Export (which also uses Default).

## Suggested fix
Give the static configuration one owner. Either have Settings own a persisted list of extra sensitive headers and document the static setters as Editor-preference-driven, or make ApplyMonitorPreferences only apply a preference when it changed and never downgrade a policy that application code installed (for example compose: user policy + preference toggle).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] MonitorInterceptor static configuration has a single owner
- [ ] ApplyMonitorPreferences applies a preference only when it changed and never downgrades a policy that application code installed (or Settings persists extra sensitive headers and the static setters are documented as preference-driven)
- [ ] A policy set in a BeforeSceneLoad initializer survives PlayModeStateChange.EnteredPlayMode
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Editor/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `util-design-04` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/util.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: architecture.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Editor/Settings/TurboHttpSettings.cs:117-122 ([InitializeOnLoad] static ctor), 124-133 (EnteredPlayMode/EnteredEditMode) and 185 call ApplyMonitorPreferences, which at 137-146 assigns every public static of MonitorInterceptor from EditorPrefs; 143-145 can only yield RedactionPolicy.Default or None. MonitorInterceptor.RedactionPolicy has a documented public setter (MonitorInterceptor.cs:139-148) and RedactionPolicy.WithSensitiveHeaders is public (RedactionPolicy.cs:91-98); Preferences has no field for extra headers (TurboHttpSettings.cs:162-173). EnteredPlayMode fires after scene Awake/BeforeSceneLoad initializers, so a policy set there is replaced and the extra header is captured in clear. Tests/Editor/HttpMonitorRedactionSettingsTests.cs:40-58 asserts only the Default/None assignment. Editor-only exposure. #117 plans one policy object but does not mention this overwrite.

Related: #117, [[R11-util-design-32]], [[R11-util-design-05]].

title: [Editor] TurboHttpBackgroundPluginGate enumerates every plugin importer in the project on each domain reload
body:
## Summary
The gate scans all plugin importers on every script recompile and Play Mode entry. The cost scales with the number of precompiled DLLs and native plugins in the project, not with this package. Large projects pay it on every domain reload.

## Location
- `Editor/TurboHttpBackgroundPluginGate.cs:52`

## Problem
The [InitializeOnLoad] static constructor calls Register() (TurboHttpBackgroundPluginGate.cs:35-38), which iterates PluginImporter.GetAllImporters() and reads assetPath of each to find two known package paths (49-62); it runs again before each build (43-46). GetAllImporters returns an importer object for every native plugin and every managed DLL of the project and its packages.

**Failure scenario.** A project with a few thousand precompiled DLLs/native plugins pays the enumeration (object creation plus a string per importer) on every script recompile and Play Mode entry with domain reload; the cost scales with the project, not with this package. Measure with the Editor profiler's domain-reload markers to confirm the magnitude.

## Suggested fix
Resolve the two importers directly (AssetImporter.GetAtPath on the package paths, falling back to the full scan only when the package is embedded elsewhere) and keep the full scan for the pre-build callback.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The two package importers are resolved directly through AssetImporter.GetAtPath on the package paths, with the full scan only as a fallback when the package lives elsewhere
- [ ] The full scan stays for the pre-build callback
- [ ] Domain-reload time on a project with thousands of plugins is measured before and after and recorded
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Editor/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `util-runtime-23` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/util.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: performance.

Verification: Not independently verified: low-severity findings were not sent to a second reviewer. Re-trace it in the code before fixing.

title: [Editor] TurboHttpBackgroundPluginGate keys native plugin inclusion on Player Settings defines, so a define passed another way compiles callers without the plugin
body:
## Summary
Plugin inclusion is decided from the active build target's Player Settings defines. A build that passes TURBOHTTP_BACKGROUND_NETWORKING another way (for example extraScriptingDefines) compiles the managed DllImport callers while the native plugin is excluded. The failure appears as a missing symbol at Xcode link time or first call on Android, far from the cause.

## Location
- `Editor/TurboHttpBackgroundPluginGate.cs:95`

## Problem
ShouldIncludeInBuild (TurboHttpBackgroundPluginGate.cs:95-99) reads PlayerSettings.GetScriptingDefineSymbolsForGroup for EditorUserBuildSettings.activeBuildTarget and ignores the BuildReport passed to OnPreprocessBuild (43-46). The class comment (13-20) states the invariant 'native code and its callers are always built in together' and then documents that defines passed through BuildPlayerOptions.extraScriptingDefines are not seen. Scripts are compiled with extraScriptingDefines, so the invariant does not hold for such builds and nothing fails the build. Register (49-62) also walks PluginImporter.GetAllImporters() on every domain reload.

**Failure scenario.** A CI script builds iOS with extraScriptingDefines = { "TURBOHTTP_BACKGROUND_NETWORKING" }: the managed bridge compiles its DllImport calls, the .mm file is excluded, and the Xcode link (or the first call on Android) fails with a missing symbol far from the cause.

## Suggested fix
Detect the mismatch and fail the build with a clear message (for example compile a marker type under the define and check for it in the player assemblies in a post-compile callback), or key inclusion on something both sides read.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A mismatch between the compiled define and plugin inclusion fails the build with a message naming the define and the plugin
- [ ] Both sides read the same source for the decision, or a post-compile check detects the mismatch
- [ ] A CI-style build passing the define through extraScriptingDefines either works or fails with that message
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Editor/ fails before the fix and passes after it
- [ ] validated on a device build and recorded

## Context

title: [Editor] TurboHttpWebGlBuildGuard fails every WebGL build while the package is installed, with no opt-out
body:
## Summary
The guard fails any WebGL player build when the package is present, although the transport is pluggable and several modules compile for WebGL. A multi-platform title shipping iOS/Android with TurboHTTP and WebGL on UnityWebRequest or a custom IHttpTransport cannot produce the WebGL build at all.

## Location
- `Editor/TurboHttpWebGlBuildGuard.cs:23`

## Problem
TurboHttpWebGlBuildGuard.cs:23-33 throws BuildFailedException for BuildTarget.WebGL unconditionally (callbackOrder -1000); the message's only remedy is removing the package. Its stated reason ('every request would fail at runtime') holds only for the default raw-socket transport: Core exposes IHttpTransport and HttpTransportFactory.Register for other transports, Transport/Complete already exclude WebGL in their asmdefs, and Runtime/Core/ProjectJsonBridge.cs:8-10 documents what 'WebGL builds' must call, i.e. Core/JSON are expected to be usable there. Tests/Editor/WebGlBuildGuardTests.cs only asserts the unconditional throw.

**Failure scenario.** A multi-platform title ships iOS/Android with TurboHTTP and a WebGL build that uses UnityWebRequest behind #if UNITY_WEBGL (or registers its own fetch-based IHttpTransport): the WebGL build cannot be produced at all while com.turbohttp.complete is in the manifest.

## Suggested fix
Keep the guard as the default but add an explicit opt-out (a scripting define such as TURBOHTTP_ALLOW_WEBGL or a project setting), and say so in the message; downgrade to a build warning when opted out.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The guard stays the default and its message names an explicit opt-out (scripting define TURBOHTTP_ALLOW_WEBGL or a project setting)
- [ ] When opted out the guard emits a build warning instead of failing
- [ ] Documentation states the opt-out and that the socket transport does not run on WebGL
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Editor/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `util-design-07` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/util.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: architecture.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Editor/TurboHttpWebGlBuildGuard.cs:23-33 throws BuildFailedException for BuildTarget.WebGL unconditionally (callbackOrder -1000), no define or setting to opt out; Tests/Editor/WebGlBuildGuardTests.cs asserts only that. A project that carries the package for iOS/Android and also has a WebGL target cannot build WebGL. This is a deliberate, documented decision, not an oversight: closed #9 asked for exactly this guard, README.md:148, Documentation~/QuickStart.md:9 and PlatformNotes.md:14 state it, and open #130 (v2.0 WebGL fetch transport) says 'Until then WebGL must fail at build time (#9)'. The guard's stated reason is correct for the default transport; what is missing is only the opt-out, which #130 does not list. Low: documented product limitation.

Related: #130.

title: [Files] DownloadOptions.ExpectedSha256 and ExpectedMd5 are silently ignored unless VerifyChecksum is also true
body:
## Summary
FileDownloader verifies a checksum only when VerifyChecksum is set; the expected hash values alone do nothing and no error is raised. A caller passing only ExpectedSha256 gets a download committed without any hash computed and believes integrity was checked. This is a silent integrity bypass for DLC and update downloads.

## Location
- `Runtime/Files/FileDownloader.cs:35`

## Problem
FileDownloader.cs:32-39 declares VerifyChecksum (default false), ExpectedMd5 and ExpectedSha256 with no XML docs. CreateHashState (657-666) enables a hash only when options.VerifyChecksum && !IsNullOrEmpty(Expected...), and VerifyHashes (705-708) returns immediately when !options.VerifyChecksum. Conversely VerifyChecksum=true with both expected values empty verifies nothing. Every test and the documentation sample set both (Tests/Runtime/Files/FileDownloaderTests.cs:142,167,191,452; Documentation~/APIReference.md:307-308); no test covers an expected hash without the flag.

**Failure scenario.** new DownloadOptions { ExpectedSha256 = manifestHash } is passed to DownloadFileAsync for a DLC file: the download completes and is committed to the destination without any hash being computed, and the caller believes integrity was checked.

## Suggested fix
Derive verification from the presence of an expected hash (obsolete or drop the flag), or throw ArgumentException when the flag and the expected values disagree. Add the missing test.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Passing ExpectedSha256 or ExpectedMd5 triggers verification without a second flag, or a conflicting flag/value combination throws ArgumentException
- [ ] A hash mismatch fails the download with a UHttpException and removes the partial file
- [ ] VerifyChecksum is obsoleted or dropped with an XML doc note
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Files/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `util-design-06` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/util.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: best-practices.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Runtime/Files/FileDownloader.cs:32-39: VerifyChecksum (default false), ExpectedMd5, ExpectedSha256 with no XML docs. CreateHashState (657-666) enables hashing only when VerifyChecksum && expected value set; VerifyHashes (705-708) returns when !VerifyChecksum. So DownloadOptions { ExpectedSha256 = h } alone commits the file unverified with no error, and VerifyChecksum = true with no expected value verifies nothing. Every use in Tests/Runtime/Files (FileDownloaderTests.cs:142,167,191,452; ResumeSafetyTests.cs:325) and Documentation~/APIReference.md:307-308 sets both; no test covers the mismatch. An integrity check that fails open on a plausible caller mistake.

Also reported as `util-protocol-22` (merged into this issue).

Related: [[R11-util-protocol-26]].

title: [Files] FileDownloader.DownloadFileAsync is a 250-line method with wall-clock timing and a culture-sensitive Content-Length parse
body:
## Summary
One method owns path validation, resume negotiation, the body pump, hashing and commit. It reads DownloadOptions live during the download, times progress with wall-clock time (negative speed after a clock sync), and parses Content-Length with the current culture.

## Location
- `Runtime/Files/FileDownloader.cs:125`

## Problem
FileDownloader.cs:125-375 is one method with five nested try/using levels. Elapsed time and speed use DateTime.UtcNow (149, 366, 645-653), so a clock adjustment during a download yields negative or inflated ElapsedTime/SpeedBytesPerSecond. Line 236 parses Content-Length with long.TryParse(string, out) (current culture, sign and whitespace accepted) while the same file parses Content-Range with NumberStyles.None and InvariantCulture (458-467, 479). options.EnableResume and options.Progress are re-read from the caller's mutable object at 158, 174, 198, 288, 310 and 354 across awaits instead of being snapshotted. BasePath protection defers symlink handling to 'a future hardening phase' (139-140) in a shipping path.

**Failure scenario.** A caller reuses one DownloadOptions and flips EnableResume between calls while a download is in flight: the first download records a validator under one setting and deletes or keeps the partial under the other; on a device whose clock syncs mid-download the progress callback reports a negative speed.

## Suggested fix

title: [Files] FileDownloader BasePath containment is a lexical prefix check: symlinks are not resolved and Apple targets compare case-insensitively

title: [Files] Failure to write the optional .part.validator sidecar aborts the whole download, so paths near the platform limit fail
body:
## Summary

Treat the validator as best effort: catch IOException/UnauthorizedAccessException/PathTooLongException around WriteValidator, make sure no validator remains, and continue without resume.

title: [Files] FileDownloader has no limit on bytes written to disk
body:
## Summary
A hostile or misconfigured server can send an endless chunked body or a Content-Length of hundreds of GB and the downloader writes until storage is full. With EnableResume (the default) the .part file is kept after the IOException, so the storage stays exhausted.

## Location
- `Runtime/Files/FileDownloader.cs:294`

## Problem
The copy loop (294-316) writes until ReadAsync returns 0. DownloadOptions (32-39) has no size limit, Content-Length is used only for progress (233-239), and streaming responses are not capped by the client (Http2Options.DefaultMaxResponseBodySize = 0; the HTTP/1.1 MaxResponseBodySize check applies to buffered bodies).

**Failure scenario.** A hostile or misconfigured server answers with an endless chunked body (or a Content-Length of several hundred GB). The download fills the device's storage; with EnableResume (default) the .part file is kept after the IOException, so the storage stays exhausted.

## Suggested fix
Add DownloadOptions.MaxBytes (and reject up front when Content-Length or the Content-Range complete-length exceeds it), fail with a UHttpException and delete the partial when the limit is crossed.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] DownloadOptions.MaxBytes exists and is documented
- [ ] A Content-Length or Content-Range complete length above MaxBytes is rejected before writing

title: [Files] FileDownloader reports progress after every body read with a new DownloadProgress and no throttling
body:
## Summary
FileDownloader calls ReportProgress after each ReadAsync and allocates a DownloadProgress object per call. With Progress<T> every report is posted to the captured SynchronizationContext. A large download produces tens of thousands of main-thread callbacks and allocations, affecting Unity apps with UI progress handlers.

## Location
- `Runtime/Files/FileDownloader.cs:310`

## Problem
The copy loop calls ReportProgress after each ReadAsync (FileDownloader.cs:296-315); ReportProgress reads DateTime.UtcNow and allocates a DownloadProgress per call (635-655). Reads return at most one transport read (typically <= 16 KB over TLS). With the standard Progress<T>, Report posts each value to the captured SynchronizationContext.

**Failure scenario.** A 1 GB download produces 30,000-65,000 reports; on a fast link that is over a thousand per second, each a main-thread callback queued through UnitySynchronizationContext (dozens run in one frame, the user's UI handler runs for each) plus the per-report allocations.

## Suggested fix
Throttle by time or bytes (for example at most every 100 ms plus a final report) and reuse or pass a struct snapshot.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Progress reports are throttled by time or bytes (for example at most one per 100 ms) plus one final report with the total
- [ ] Per-report allocation is removed (struct snapshot or reused object) or documented as the public contract

title: [Files] FileDownloader commits the .part file by rename without flushing to stable storage
body:
## Summary
FileDownloader flushes the managed buffer with FlushAsync but never fsyncs before renaming the partial file onto the destination. After power loss or an OS crash the destination can be empty or short while the .part and validator are gone, so later runs treat it as complete. Mobile devices are most exposed.

## Location
- `Runtime/Files/FileDownloader.cs:323`

## Problem
The body is flushed with fileStream.FlushAsync (FileDownloader.cs:323), which empties the managed buffer but does not fsync; the stream is closed and CommitPartFile renames/replaces it (359, 588-594) and the validator is deleted. Nothing calls Flush(true) on the file or syncs the directory.

**Failure scenario.** Android/iOS device loses power (or the OS crashes) shortly after a large download returns: on filesystems with delayed allocation the renamed destination can be empty or short, and later runs treat it as a complete file because the .part and validator are gone and no checksum is re-verified.

## Suggested fix
Call fileStream.Flush(flushToDisk: true) before closing the partial when committing (optionally behind an option for callers who prefer speed), and document the durability level.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The partial file is flushed to disk (Flush(true)) before the commit rename, optionally behind a DownloadOptions setting

title: [Files] FileDownloader has no per-destination exclusion, so concurrent downloads to one path corrupt each other's .part and validator
body:
## Summary
The .part and validator paths derive only from the destination and are inspected, deleted and opened without any lock. A second concurrent download to the same path deletes the first one's validator and, on POSIX semantics, its open partial file. The first download then fails at commit after transferring the whole body, or the second fails with a raw IOException.

## Location
- `Runtime/Files/FileDownloader.cs:354`

## Problem
The partial and validator paths are derived only from the destination (FileDownloader.cs:150-151) and are inspected, deleted and opened with no lock or in-progress marker: the resume probe reads the other call's growing .part length (158-168), line 253 deletes the validator before the truncating open, the FileStream is opened with FileShare.None (271-278), and the finally at 351-356 deletes both files when the call did not complete and EnableResume is false.

**Failure scenario.** Call A is downloading to X (resume enabled); call B starts for the same X with EnableResume=false: B deletes A's validator (line 253), fails to open X.part, and its finally calls File.Delete on A's open partial. Where deleting an open file is allowed (POSIX semantics under IL2CPP on iOS/Android; needs a device run to confirm the runtime's share emulation) A keeps writing to an unlinked file and fails at CommitPartFile after transferring the whole body. With defaults B issues a wasted Range request and then fails with a raw IOException.

## Suggested fix
Track in-flight destinations in a static concurrent set (or hold an exclusive lock file) and fail fast with a clear exception; delete partial files in the finally only when this call opened them.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Concurrent DownloadFileAsync calls to the same destination fail fast with a clear exception (or are serialized) instead of touching the other call's files
- [ ] The finally block deletes partial and validator files only when this call opened them

title: [Files] FileDownloader resume records a validator and offset for a transparently decoded body, poisoning the partial
body:
## Summary
With EnableResume the request sends Accept-Encoding: identity, but a server may still return a content-coded body that DecompressionHandler decodes and strips headers from. FileDownloader then stores the ETag and a decoded byte count, and later sends Range with an offset that refers to the encoded representation. The resumed 206 is a mid-stream fragment, decoding fails, and the partial is kept, so the download can never succeed without manual cleanup.

## Location
- `Runtime/Files/FileDownloader.cs:385`

## Problem
With EnableResume the request carries Accept-Encoding: identity (385-390), but a server may still send a coded representation (objects stored with Content-Encoding: gzip metadata on S3-style storage ignore Accept-Encoding). DecompressionHandler then decodes it and strips Content-Encoding and Content-Length before FileDownloader sees the response (Runtime/Middleware/DecompressionHandler.cs:77-79), so SelectStrongValidator stores the ETag (286-288) and the .part length counts decoded bytes. The next attempt sends Range: bytes=<decoded length>- against the encoded representation; the 206 is a mid-stream gzip fragment that DecompressionHandler cannot inflate.

**Failure scenario.** Download of a gzip-stored asset is interrupted at decoded offset N smaller than the encoded size. Every later DownloadFileAsync call sends the same Range, gets a 206 fragment, fails with a decompression error before any cleanup, and keeps the .part and validator: the download cannot succeed until the files are deleted by hand.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 14.2

## Suggested fix
Make the downloader's requests opt out of transparent decoding (a request flag the decompression interceptor honours) so offsets always refer to wire bytes, or do not record a validator when the response was content-coded; on a failed resumed attempt that is not a cancellation, discard the partial.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Downloader requests opt out of transparent decoding, or no validator is recorded when the response was content-coded, so resume offsets always refer to wire bytes
- [ ] A failed resumed attempt that is not a cancellation discards the partial and validator
- [ ] Regression test in Tests/Runtime/Files/ interrupts a gzip-coded download and asserts the next call completes with correct bytes instead of failing repeatedly

title: [Files] FileDownloader appends a 206 without confirming a Last-Modified validator or binding the partial to its URL
body:
## Summary
IsResumableContinuation compares validators only when the stored validator is an entity-tag and the 206 carries an ETag; a stored Last-Modified is never compared and a 206 without ETag is accepted. The validator sidecar does not record the URL, so a different URL downloaded to the same path resumes onto the earlier partial. A server or CDN that ignores If-Range can cause a file mixing two representations to be committed (RFC 9110 section 15.3.7.3).

## Location
- `Runtime/Files/FileDownloader.cs:409`

## Problem
IsResumableContinuation compares validators only when the stored one is an entity-tag AND the 206 carries an ETag (421-426); a stored Last-Modified validator is never compared with the 206's Last-Modified, and a 206 without ETag is accepted. The sidecar holds only the validator string (WriteValidator 577-586), not the URL it belongs to, so DownloadFileAsync(urlB, samePath) reuses urlA's partial (158-168). RFC 9110 section 15.3.7.3 allows combining partial responses only when they share the same strong validator; the code relies entirely on the server honouring If-Range.

**Failure scenario.** (1) A server or CDN edge that implements Range but ignores If-Range answers 206 from offset N of a changed representation; with a Last-Modified validator (or no ETag in the 206) the bytes are appended and a file mixing two versions is committed (no checksum configured). (2) Two URLs whose representations share a Last-Modified second (same deploy) are downloaded to the same destination; the second resumes onto the first's partial.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 15.3.7.3

## Suggested fix
Require the 206 to repeat the stored validator (ETag equal, or Last-Modified equal when the stored validator is a date) and restart otherwise; store the request URL (or its hash) in the validator sidecar and discard the partial when it differs.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A 206 must repeat the stored validator (ETag equal, or Last-Modified equal for a date validator); otherwise the download restarts from zero
- [ ] The validator sidecar stores the request URL (or its hash) and the partial is discarded when the URL differs
- [ ] Regression test in Tests/Runtime/Files/ covers a 206 with a different Last-Modified, a 206 without ETag, and a different URL for the same destination

title: [Files] MultipartFormDataBuilder buffers every file in memory and copies it into a pooled writer capped at 64 MiB
body:
## Summary
AddFileFromDisk reads the whole file synchronously, and ApplyTo writes all parts into a PooledArrayBufferWriter that grows by copying and throws above 64 MiB. A 40 MB mobile upload peaks near 136 MB with LOH allocations and a main-thread hitch, and a 70 MB file throws from ApplyTo while Build() succeeds. The cost is about three times the file size.

## Location
- `Runtime/Files/MultipartFormDataBuilder.cs:171`

## Problem
AddFileFromDisk reads the file with File.ReadAllBytes on the calling thread (MultipartFormDataBuilder.cs:96). ApplyTo -> BuildAsOwner -> WriteTo writes all parts into a `new PooledArrayBufferWriter()` that starts at 256 bytes (142-155, 171-176); the writer grows by copying (double to 1 MiB, then x1.5) and throws InvalidOperationException above MaxBufferSize = 64 MiB (Runtime/Core/Internal/PooledArrayBufferWriter.cs:44, 204-235). ByteArrayPool is ArrayPool<byte>.Shared (ByteArrayPool.cs:56), which does not pool arrays above 1 MiB, so each growth step above that is a fresh LOH allocation dropped on return. The total length is computable up front (part headers + data lengths) but no size hint is passed, and there is no streaming multipart body although FileRequestBody shows the streaming model exists. Build() (MemoryStream, 104-117) has no 64 MiB limit, so the two public paths behave differently.

Add a multipart UHttpRequestBody that streams parts (known Content-Length, files opened per read session like FileRequestBody); at minimum compute the exact body length first and request it once from the writer, and document or lift the 64 MiB limit consistently for Build and ApplyTo.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Peak memory for a single large file upload is bounded by a buffer size, not by file size; state the measured peak and LOH allocations before and after

title: [Files] Multipart names and filenames are backslash-escaped instead of percent-encoded and control characters are not rejected
body:
## Summary
EscapeQuotedString escapes quote and backslash with a backslash, while browsers (WHATWG encoding that RFC 7578 defers to) send %22 and %0D%0A and many server parsers do not unescape backslashes. ValidateNoCrLf lets NUL and other C0 controls through. A filename containing a quote can be truncated by the server and one with NUL can reach servers that truncate at NUL.

## Location
- `Runtime/Files/MultipartFormDataBuilder.cs:182`

## Problem
EscapeQuotedString turns '"' into '\"' and '\' into '\\' (182-185), cited as RFC 2616 quoted-string; the class summary says this is what 'RFC 7578 sections 4.2 and 5.1.1 and browsers do'. Browsers (WHATWG multipart/form-data encoding, which RFC 7578 defers to in practice) send %22 for '"' and %0D%0A for line breaks and leave backslashes alone, and many server parsers do not unescape backslashes. ValidateNoCrLf (190-195) lets NUL and other C0 controls through.

**Failure scenario.** A filename 'report "final".txt' is sent as filename="report \"final\".txt"; a parser that follows the browser convention ends the value at the first inner quote and stores 'report \' (or rejects the part). A filename containing NUL reaches servers that truncate at NUL ('a.php\0.png').

## Spec reference
RFC 7578 4.2

## Suggested fix
Encode '"' as %22 (and optionally backslash unchanged) as browsers do, reject characters below 0x20 and 0x7F in names and filenames, and correct the summary. Confirm against the target servers' parsers (Go mime/multipart, PHP, busboy).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Quote in names and filenames is encoded as %22 as browsers do, and the class summary is corrected
- [ ] Characters below 0x20 and 0x7F are rejected in names and filenames
- [ ] Regression test in Tests/Runtime/Files/ covers a filename with quotes, backslashes and NUL
- [ ] Behaviour confirmed against Go mime/multipart, PHP and busboy parsers

title: [JSON] JSON bridge forwards internal DOM parsing to the replaceable JsonSerializer.Default, breaking RecordReplayTransport and OAuth parsing with a custom serializer
body:
## Summary
The only IJsonBridge implementation calls JsonSerializer.Default, which users are told to replace with Newtonsoft or System.Text.Json adapters. Internal consumers such as RecordReplayTransport and OAuth token parsing require LiteJson's DOM types (Dictionary<string, object>, List<object>). With a custom serializer recording redacts every JSON body and replay loads zero entries.

## Location
- `Runtime/JSON/JsonModuleRegistration.cs:34`

## Problem
JsonModuleRegistration.cs:32-37: the only IJsonBridge implementation calls JsonSerializer.Serialize/Deserialize, i.e. JsonSerializer.Default (JsonSerializer.cs:43-53), which documentation tells users to replace (JsonSerializer.cs:23-28, LiteJsonSerializer.cs:41-46). Internal consumers need LiteJson's DOM shape: RecordReplayTransport.Serialization.cs:105-112 loads entries only when the value 'is List<object>' and otherwise leaves Entries empty without an error, 90-93 requires the root to be Dictionary<string, object>; RecordReplayTransport.Redaction.cs:242-285 returns false for any node that is not Dictionary<string,object>/List<object>/primitive and the caller then stores the placeholder (119-149, 194-199); Runtime/Auth/OAuthClient.cs:437-441 does 'result as Dictionary<string, object> ?? new Dictionary' (empty on any other shape). Tests/Runtime/Testing/RecordReplayRedactionTests.cs:104-116 covers only the fail-closed redaction path with a fake serializer; no test loads a recording under a non-Lite serializer. The design also stacks two static registries (ProjectJsonBridge -> JsonSerializer.Default) behind a single-implementation internal interface, and errors are wrapped twice (ProjectJsonBridge.cs:75-80 and RecordReplayTransport.Serialization.cs:258-282 both wrap in InvalidOperationException).

**Failure scenario.** Project calls JsonSerializer.SetDefault(new NewtonsoftAdapter()). Record mode: every JSON request/response body parses to a JObject, TryRedactJsonNode returns false and the body is recorded as "[REDACTED]". Replay mode: the file's "Entries" deserializes to a JArray, 'is List<object>' is false, LoadRecordings returns with zero entries and every request fails with 'No replay recording matched request key' (or silently hits the network under Warn/Relaxed).

## Suggested fix
Split the bridge contract: a DOM pair (parse to Dictionary<string,object>/List<object>, write the same) bound to LiteJsonSerializer.Instance regardless of JsonSerializer.Default, and a typed pair that follows Default for user payloads (MockResponseBuilder.Json<T>, WithJsonBody<T>, WebSocket messages). Make FromSerializableObject throw when Entries has an unexpected shape.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The bridge splits into a DOM pair bound to LiteJsonSerializer.Instance regardless of JsonSerializer.Default, and a typed pair that follows Default for user payloads
- [ ] RecordReplayTransport.FromSerializableObject throws when Entries has an unexpected shape
- [ ] Regression test in Tests/Runtime/Core/ (or JSON) sets a non-Lite default serializer and asserts record and replay round-trip and OAuth token parsing still work

## Context

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: The single IJsonBridge forwards to the user-replaceable JsonSerializer.Default (Runtime/JSON/JsonModuleRegistration.cs:32-37; JsonSerializer.cs:23-28,43-53 advertise Newtonsoft). Internal consumers require LiteJson's DOM: RecordReplayTransport.Serialization.cs:105-112 fills Entries only when the value 'is List<object>' and otherwise returns an empty recording without error (a Newtonsoft-style adapter returns Dictionary<string, object> at the root, passing line 90, with a JArray for Entries); RecordReplayTransport.Redaction.cs:124-136,242-285 returns the placeholder for any non-Dictionary/List node, so every JSON body is recorded as [REDACTED]. That redaction fallback is deliberate fail-closed (comment 239-241, test RecordReplayRedactionTests.cs:105-117), but the silent empty load is not guarded and no test loads a recording under a non-Lite serializer. The OAuth part is weaker: OAuthClient.cs:437-441 gets a real Dictionary<string, object> from a Newtonsoft-style adapter for a flat token response, so it breaks only for adapters returning another root type or element wrappers. Outcome depends on the user's adapter, but the documented one triggers it.

title: [JSON] WithJsonBody and the multipart ApplyTo leak the detached pooled buffer when attaching it to the request throws
body:
## Summary
WithJsonBody detaches the writer's buffer and then calls WithLeasedBody inside a try whose catch only disposes the writer, which is a no-op after detaching. If the request is null or disposed, the rented array is never returned to ArrayPool. ByteArrayPool.ActiveCount drifts by one per call. MultipartFormDataBuilder.ApplyTo has the same gap.

## Location
- `Runtime/JSON/JsonRequestBuilderExtensions.cs:35`

## Problem
WithJsonBody detaches the writer (`writer.DetachAsOwner()`) and then calls `request.WithLeasedBody(owner, ...)` inside the same try (JsonRequestBuilderExtensions.cs:35-36, 66-67, 91-92, 115-116); the catch only calls writer.Dispose(), which is a no-op for a detached writer (PooledArrayBufferWriter.cs:143-163), so the owner is never disposed. WithLeasedBody throws ObjectDisposedException for a disposed request before taking ownership (Runtime/Core/UHttpRequest.cs:245-254) and a null `request` throws NullReferenceException at the same point. MultipartFormDataBuilder.ApplyTo has the same gap with no try at all (MultipartFormDataBuilder.cs:174-175).

**Failure scenario.** Calling WithJsonBody on a request that was already sent/disposed (or null) serialises the whole payload, then throws and drops the rented array: it is never returned to ArrayPool and ByteArrayPool's ActiveCount (the soak leak oracle) drifts by one per call.

## Suggested fix
Validate the request (null/disposed) before serialising, and dispose the detached owner in the catch (keep it in a local and null it after WithLeasedBody succeeds).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The request is validated (null, disposed) before serialising
- [ ] The detached owner is disposed on every failure path and ownership transfers exactly once
- [ ] Regression test in Tests/Runtime/Core/ calls WithJsonBody and ApplyTo on a disposed request and asserts ByteArrayPool.ActiveCount is unchanged

## Summary

No shadow-build variant defines it, so it is never compiled by the gates, and TurboHTTP.JSON.asmdef has no reference to System.Text.Json. title: [JSON] LiteJson JsonReader uses the default string comparer for objects, allowing hash-collision flooding
body:
## Summary
JsonReader.ReadObject inserts every member into a Dictionary<string, object> with the default string comparer and has no member cap. On Unity's Mono and IL2CPP class libraries string hashing is deterministic, so a hostile endpoint can send colliding keys within the 16 MiB input cap and force quadratic insertion time. Applications parsing untrusted JSON via AsJson, OAuth token parsing or recording redaction are affected.

## Location
- `Runtime/JSON/LiteJson/JsonReader.cs:124`

## Problem
ReadObject creates new Dictionary<string, object>() (124) and inserts every member with dict[key] = value (140). There is no cap on members per object and no collision counting; the only bounds are MaxDepth 64 (23) and MaxInputBytes 16 MiB (LiteJsonSerializer.cs:150-155). On Unity's Mono/IL2CPP class library string.GetHashCode is deterministic and not per-process randomised, and the Dictionary does not switch to a randomised comparer on collisions as CoreCLR does, so colliding keys can be precomputed. The fuzz/hardening tests (Tests/Runtime/JSON) have no collision case.

**Failure scenario.** A compromised or third-party endpoint returns a 2-16 MB JSON object whose 10^5-10^6 short keys all hash to the same bucket. AsJson<Dictionary<string, object>>() (or any AsJson<object>, OAuth token parsing and RecordReplay redaction through ProjectJsonBridge) performs about n^2/2 string comparisons: tens of seconds at 10^5 keys, hours at 10^6, pinning a thread-pool thread or the main thread of the game.

## Spec reference
RFC 8259 4

## Suggested fix
Use a comparer seeded with a per-process random value (seeded FNV-1a/Marvin-style IEqualityComparer<string>) for dictionaries built from parsed input, and/or cap members per object and total nodes per document with a JsonParseException. Confirm on a Unity 2021.3 Mono and IL2CPP player by parsing a generated colliding-key document.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Objects parsed by JsonReader use a per-process randomized comparer and/or a documented member-count limit that throws JsonParseException when exceeded
- [ ] A document with 10^5 pre-computed colliding keys parses in time linear in its size or is rejected with JsonParseException
- [ ] a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/JSON/ fails before the fix and passes after it
- [ ] Behaviour on a Unity 2021.3 Mono and IL2CPP player confirmed with a generated colliding-key document and recorded

## Context

Verification: Plausible: the code is as described; the outcome depends on runtime, device or peer behaviour that a static review cannot settle.

Verifier note: Code is as described: ReadObject builds new Dictionary<string, object>() and inserts every member with no member or node cap (JsonReader.cs:121-140); only MaxDepth 64 (JsonReader.cs:23) and MaxInputBytes 16 MiB (LiteJsonSerializer.cs:150-155) bound the input. Whether this is quadratic depends on whether string hashing in Unity 2021.3's Mono/IL2CPP class library is deterministic and whether its Dictionary falls back to a randomized comparer; that cannot be settled from this repository and no test covers it. Needs a hostile or compromised server and a caller that parses to Dictionary<string, object>; client-side CPU DoS only.

title: [JSON] LiteJson JsonReader has no node budget: 16 MiB of empty containers allocates about 500 MB
body:
## Summary
JsonReader bounds only input bytes (16 MiB) and nesting depth (64). Each '{}' allocates a Dictionary and each '[]' a List, so a small hostile document expands to hundreds of megabytes of heap. A malicious server can exhaust memory and get a mobile app killed by the OS.

## Location
- `Runtime/JSON/LiteJson/JsonReader.cs:158`

## Problem
Every '{}' allocates a Dictionary<string, object> (ReadObject 124) and every '[]' a List<object> (ReadArray 161); every integer is boxed (363-368). There is no node/element budget. '{},' costs 3 input bytes and about 80-100 bytes of heap on 64-bit Mono/IL2CPP (object header plus Dictionary fields, plus the parent list slot and List growth copies); '0,' costs 2 bytes and a 24-byte box plus an 8-byte slot.

**Failure scenario.** A hostile server sends '[' + '{},' x 5.5 million + '{}]' (16 MiB, or far less on the wire with gzip, up to the 32 MB decoded cap of DecompressionInterceptor). Deserialisation allocates on the order of 500 MB and the app is killed by the OS on a mobile device.

## Suggested fix
Add a node budget to JsonReader (containers plus scalars, default proportional to a memory target, e.g. 1-2 million) that throws JsonParseException, and expose it next to MaxInputBytes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] JsonReader enforces a configurable node budget (containers plus scalars) and throws JsonParseException when it is exceeded
- [ ] The budget is exposed next to MaxInputBytes with a documented default
- [ ] a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/JSON/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [JSON] LiteJson JsonReader appends string chars one at a time and allocates a substring per number
body:
## Summary
ReadString copies each character through a StringBuilder even when the string has no escapes, and ReadNumber allocates a substring per number before TryParse. This causes avoidable allocations and copies when parsing numeric arrays or large base64 strings.

## Location
- `Runtime/JSON/LiteJson/JsonReader.cs:359`

## Problem
ReadString copies every character with `_stringBuffer.Append(c)` and then ToString() (JsonReader.cs:191-237), also for strings without escapes that could be taken with one Substring; ReadNumber allocates `_json.Substring(start, _position - start)` for each number before long/ulong/double.TryParse (359-376) although the span-based TryParse overloads exist in .NET Standard 2.1. Each scalar is additionally boxed by design.

**Failure scenario.** Parsing a 1 MB response of numeric arrays allocates one short-lived string per number (tens of thousands of objects); loading a recording with multi-megabyte base64 strings performs millions of Append(char) calls and copies each string twice.

## Suggested fix
Scan to the closing quote and Substring when no escape was seen (fall back to the builder on the first backslash), and parse numbers from `_json.AsSpan(start, length)`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ReadString returns a single Substring when no escape sequence is present and falls back to the builder at the first backslash
- [ ] ReadNumber parses long, ulong and double from a ReadOnlySpan<char> without allocating a substring
- [ ] Parsing a numeric array of 10,000 numbers allocates no per-number string (measured allocation count recorded in the PR)
- [ ] a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/JSON/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [JSON] LiteJson rejects the whole document when one integer exceeds ulong.MaxValue or a float exceeds double range
body:
## Summary
ReadNumber tries long, then ulong, then throws 'Integer out of range' without falling back to double, and throws 'Invalid number' for out-of-range exponents such as 1e400. A response containing one big integer field fails to parse entirely even if the caller needs only other fields. Newtonsoft and System.Text.Json accept the same text.

## Location
- `Runtime/JSON/LiteJson/JsonReader.cs:361`

## Problem
For a token without fraction/exponent ReadNumber tries long, then ulong, then throws 'Integer out of range' (361-370); it never falls back to double. The exponent path throws 'Invalid number' when double.TryParse fails (373-376), which on Mono is the case for out-of-range magnitudes such as 1e400. Tests cover up to ulong.MaxValue only (JsonReaderTests.cs:45, LiteJsonHardeningTests.cs:338-349).

**Failure scenario.** A backend written in Python/Ruby/Go big-int serialises {"id":7,"balanceWei":1000000000000000000000}. AsJson<Dictionary<string, object>>() throws JsonSerializationException for the whole response even though the caller only needs 'id'; JavaScript, Newtonsoft and System.Text.Json (as double/decimal) accept the same text.

## Spec reference
RFC 8259 6

## Suggested fix
RFC 8259 section 6 allows range limits, but for interoperability fall back to double for integers outside the 64-bit range (precision loss is what section 6 anticipates) and map overflowing exponents to a documented outcome instead of failing the document; keep exact long/ulong where they fit.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Integers outside the 64-bit range parse as double (RFC 8259 section 6 allows range limits) while integers that fit keep exact long/ulong

title: [JSON] LiteJson number parse errors embed the whole unbounded number token in the exception message
body:
## Summary
ReadNumber puts the full number token into JsonParseException messages, and LiteJsonSerializer wraps that message again. A response with millions of digits produces several huge strings on the failure path, which are commonly logged by applications.

## Location
- `Runtime/JSON/LiteJson/JsonReader.cs:370`

## Problem
ReadNumber takes numStr = _json.Substring(start, ...) of unbounded length (359) and throws JsonParseException($"Integer out of range '{numStr}'") / $"Invalid number '{numStr}'" (370, 376); LiteJsonSerializer wraps it as $"JSON parse error: {parseError.Message}" (LiteJsonSerializer.cs:198-199).

**Failure scenario.** A response consisting of 16 million digits produces three 16M-char strings (about 100 MB of UTF-16) on the failure path, and the message is typically passed to Debug.LogError by application code, freezing the Editor console or bloating the device log.

## Suggested fix
Report the position and at most a short prefix of the token (for example the first 32 characters and its length).

- [ ] JsonParseException messages for numbers report the position, the token length and at most a 32-character prefix

title: [JSON] Public surface inconsistent: public JsonReader/JsonWriter, dead prettyPrint, HasCustomSerializer, TryAsJson swallows
body:
## Summary
JsonReader, JsonWriter and JsonParseException are public although only LiteJsonSerializer uses them, the prettyPrint option can never be enabled, and HasCustomSerializer returns true once the bootstrap installs JsonUtilitySerializer. TryAsJson also swallows exceptions such as ArgumentNullException and those from adapters. This widens the committed API and makes custom serializer registration checks unreliable.

## Location
- `Runtime/JSON/LiteJson/JsonWriter.cs:13`

## Problem
JsonWriter (JsonWriter.cs:13) and JsonReader (JsonReader.cs:21) are public sealed types; the only constructions in the package are LiteJsonSerializer.cs:102 and 164, so the prettyPrint constructor parameter (JsonWriter.cs:22) is never true and JsonParseException (JsonReader.cs:439) never escapes the serializer (wrapped at LiteJsonSerializer.cs:198-199). JsonSerializer.HasCustomSerializer (JsonSerializer.cs:129-132) returns true for the bootstrap-installed JsonUtilitySerializer. The Default setter takes a lock around a single volatile write (43-53). JsonExtensions.TryAsJson (JsonExtensions.cs:57-74) catches ArgumentNullException, which hides a null response and any ArgumentNullException thrown inside a serializer, and relies on third-party serializers wrapping their own exception types in JsonSerializationException. Failures surface as three unrelated types (NotSupportedException, JsonSerializationException, InvalidOperationException from the bridge).

**Failure scenario.** A Newtonsoft adapter that lets JsonReaderException propagate makes TryAsJson throw instead of returning false; code that checks HasCustomSerializer() to decide whether to install its serializer skips installation because the bootstrap already replaced LiteJson.

## Suggested fix
Make the Lite reader/writer internal (or commit to them with docs and a reachable pretty-print option), rename or split HasCustomSerializer, and have TryAsJson validate the argument up front and catch a documented exception contract.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] JsonReader, JsonWriter and JsonParseException are internal, or documented as public API with a reachable pretty-print option
- [ ] HasCustomSerializer is renamed or split so it reports whether a user-supplied serializer is installed, not the bootstrap default
- [ ] TryAsJson validates its argument up front and documents which exceptions it converts to false

title: [JSON] LiteJson and WithJsonBody copy bodies through extra byte[] on a false claim that span Encoding overloads are missing
body:
## Summary
Comments state that Encoding.GetBytes(ReadOnlySpan<char>, Span<byte>) is not available on .NET Standard 2.1, yet the API exists and is used elsewhere in the package. As a result WithJsonBody allocates a temporary byte[] for the whole body and AsJson on a single-segment response copies the body before decoding.

## Location
- `Runtime/JSON/LiteJson/LiteJsonSerializer.cs:236`

## Problem
LiteJsonSerializer.cs:219-221 and 236-243, and JsonRequestBuilderExtensions.cs:23-33, state that Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(ReadOnlySpan<char>, Span<byte>) is '.NET Core 2.1+ only and not available on .NET Standard 2.1 / Unity IL2CPP', then call GetByteCount, allocate a full byte[] with GetBytes(string) and copy it into the writer span. The API is part of .NET Standard 2.1, and the same slice already compiles span overloads of the same API family (HttpMonitorEvent.cs:226 GetString(ReadOnlySpan<byte>), LoggingInterceptor.cs:116, MockHttpServer.cs:516); the array overload GetBytes(string,int,int,byte[],int) used in Transport/Http2/HpackEncoder.cs:186 would also avoid the copy. LiteJsonSerializer.cs:265 does input.First.Span.ToArray() only to call GetString(byte[],...). ## Summary

Decode with `Encoding.UTF8.GetString(input.First.Span)` (or MemoryMarshal.TryGetArray) and keep the pooled path for multi-segment input.

title: [JSON] LiteJsonSerializer type support asymmetric: enum/char unreadable, Uri unwritable, fractions truncated for ints
body:
## Summary
IsSupportedTarget accepts enums and char, but conversion has no branch for them, so Deserialize<MyEnum> throws although Serialize writes enums as numbers. Uri is documented as supported but cannot be written, and Deserialize<int>("1.9") silently returns 1. Callers get inconsistent round-trips and silent data loss.

## Location
- `Runtime/JSON/LiteJson/LiteJsonSerializer.cs:308`

## Problem
IsSupportedTarget returns true for type.IsPrimitive (includes char) and type.IsEnum (308-320), but ConvertPrimitive/ConvertInt64 have no enum or char branch (387-413, 471-527), so the call ends in JsonSerializationException 'Cannot convert Int64 to MyEnum'. JsonWriter writes enums as numbers and char as a string (JsonWriter.cs:62-64, 122-124), and JsonUtilitySerializer routes enums to LiteJson as a 'built-in shape' (Runtime/Bootstrap/JsonUtilitySerializer.cs:38-41, 305-316). The class remarks list Uri among supported types (16-17) and Deserialize<Uri> works (520-521), but JsonWriter has no Uri case and throws NotSupportedException (JsonWriter.cs:138-139). ConvertDouble casts with checked((int)d) (449-459), which truncates 1.9 to 1 without error. No test covers enum/char reads, Uri writes or fractional-to-integer conversion.

**Failure scenario.** Serialize(MyEnum.B) gives '1' but Deserialize<MyEnum>("1") throws; WithJsonBody(new Dictionary<string, object>{["link"] = new Uri(..)}) throws NotSupportedException; Deserialize<int>("1.9") returns 1.

## Suggested fix
Add enum (from number and name) and char conversions or remove them from IsSupportedTarget so the caller gets the NotSupportedException with advice; write Uri as its AbsoluteUri/OriginalString; reject a non-integral double for integer targets with JsonSerializationException.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Enums are readable from numbers (and names if documented) and char from a one-character string, or both are removed from IsSupportedTarget so the caller gets NotSupportedException

title: [Observability] HttpMetrics exposes public mutable long counters (torn reads on 32-bit IL2CPP); RequestsByHost unbounded
body:
## Summary
The counters are public fields justified by a claim that Interlocked cannot work with property backing fields, which is wrong. Consumers can write any field and read 64-bit values non-atomically on ARMv7, and RequestsByHost keeps one entry per host forever.

## Location
- `Runtime/Observability/HttpMetrics.cs:16`

## Problem
HttpMetrics.cs:15-21 justifies public long fields with 'Interlocked requires ref to field, which doesn't work with property backing fields'; private fields with read-only properties using Interlocked.Read would work, and the class itself does exactly that for AverageResponseTimeMsBits (25-37) 'for atomicity on 32-bit IL2CPP'. Consumers read metrics.TotalBytesReceived directly, a non-atomic 64-bit read on ARMv7, and can write any field. MetricsInterceptor.cs:34 adds one RequestsByHost entry per distinct request.Uri.Host with no cap; with Metrics placed inside a redirect interceptor each redirect hop host is recorded. HttpMetrics is also an unsealed public class.

**Failure scenario.** On a 32-bit Android player a HUD reads TotalBytesReceived while a transfer crosses a 4 GB boundary and displays a value that is wrong by 4 GB; a long-running client that follows redirects through many generated subdomains keeps every host string for the life of the interceptor.

## Suggested fix
Make the fields private with Interlocked-backed read-only properties (or a snapshot struct), seal the class, and cap RequestsByHost (for example an 'other' bucket after N hosts).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Counters are private with read-only properties backed by Interlocked.Read, or exposed through a snapshot struct; the class is sealed
- [ ] RequestsByHost is capped (for example an 'other' bucket after N hosts) with the limit documented
- [ ] a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Observability/ fails before the fix and passes after it
- [ ] Documentation and samples use the new accessors

title: [Observability] HttpMetrics readers see torn or stale values: public 64-bit fields and a racing stored average
body:
## Summary
Request and byte counters are public long fields read directly by docs and samples, which is a non-atomic read on 32-bit IL2CPP. The stored average is overwritten by concurrent completions, so an older value can replace a newer one until another request completes.

## Location
- `Runtime/Observability/HttpMetrics.cs:17`

## Problem
TotalRequests, SuccessfulRequests, FailedRequests, TotalBytesReceived and TotalBytesSent are public long fields (HttpMetrics.cs:17-21) written with Interlocked; only the average has an Interlocked.Read accessor (27-31). The documentation and sample read the fields directly (Documentation~/Modules/Interceptors.md:184-185, Samples~/05-AdvancedFeatures/AdvancedFeaturesExample.cs:129-131), which is a non-atomic 64-bit read on 32-bit IL2CPP (ARMv7). RecordCompletion adds to the total, increments the count and then stores total/count as three separate steps (MetricsInterceptor.cs:49-55), so two completing requests can store their averages in the opposite order.

**Failure scenario.** ARMv7 Android: a UI thread reads TotalBytesReceived while a transfer thread carries the counter across a 4 GiB boundary and gets a value off by 4 GiB. Any platform: the last two requests of a burst complete concurrently and the older average overwrites the newer one, so GetAverageResponseTimeMs() stays wrong until another request completes.

## Suggested fix
Expose read-only properties or a Snapshot() that use Interlocked.Read, point the docs and sample at them, and compute the average on read from the two Interlocked counters instead of storing it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Read access to counters uses Interlocked.Read via properties or a Snapshot()
- [ ] The average response time is computed on read from Interlocked counters, not stored by racing writers
- [ ] Documentation~/Modules/Interceptors.md and the AdvancedFeatures sample use the new accessors
- [ ] a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Observability/ fails before the fix and passes after it using concurrent completions

title: [Observability] LoggingInterceptor with no sink still redacts URLs and builds every log message before discarding it
body:
## Summary
A null log delegate becomes a no-op while the level stays Standard, so every request builds redacted URLs, request and response messages and handlers that nobody receives. This costs roughly ten allocations per request for a documented 'discard' configuration.

Treat a null sink as LogLevel.None in the constructor, and skip RedactUrl when the URL has no query and no user-info.

title: [Observability] LoggingInterceptor writes body previews and error messages without escaping CR/LF or control characters
body:
## Summary
LoggingHandler appends up to 500 peer-controlled bytes of the request and response body, and error.Message, to the log line as decoded UTF-8. Nothing escapes newline, carriage return or ESC, and binary bodies are decoded as well. A server can forge additional log records or inject ANSI escape sequences into a terminal sink. Users who enable LogLevel.Detailed with logBody are affected.

## Location
- `Runtime/Observability/LoggingInterceptor.cs:159`

## Problem
FormatResponseBodyPreview decodes up to 500 peer-controlled bytes as UTF-8 and appends them to the log line as is (159-166, used at LoggingHandler.cs:156-163); the request preview does the same (LoggingInterceptor.cs:113-119); LogError appends error.Message (LoggingHandler.cs:229). Nothing escapes '\n', '\r' or ESC. Binary bodies are decoded too (no binary check, unlike HttpMonitorEvent.IsLikelyBinaryPayload).

**Failure scenario.** With LogLevel.Detailed and logBody: true a server answers with a body starting 'ok\n[TurboHTTP][ERROR] X GET https://bank.example/ -> ERROR ...'. The sink receives one message that renders as a forged second log record; ANSI escape sequences in the body reach a terminal sink.

## Suggested fix
Escape control characters (at least CR, LF, ESC, NUL) in body previews and error text before appending, and print a '<binary N bytes>' marker for bodies that fail the binary heuristic.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Body previews and error text logged by LoggingInterceptor escape CR, LF, ESC and NUL (for example as \n, \r, \x1b), so one log call yields one log line.
- [ ] Bodies that fail the binary heuristic are logged as a '<binary N bytes>' marker instead of decoded text.
- [ ] Deterministic NUnit regression test in Tests/Runtime/Observability/ with a body containing a forged log line and ESC sequences, failing before the fix.

title: [Observability] MetricsHandler allocates two delegates per request even when the response body is buffered
body:
## Summary
The MetricsHandler constructor always creates the chunk-read and body-dispose delegates, but they are used only on the streaming branch. Together with the per-request handler this costs three heap objects (about 180 bytes) per request for buffered responses and failed requests. Production clients with metrics enabled pay this on every request.

## Location
- `Runtime/Observability/MetricsHandler.cs:35`

## Problem
The MetricsHandler constructor always creates `_onObservedChunkRead = OnObservedChunkRead` and `_onObservedBodyDispose = OnObservedBodyDispose` (MetricsHandler.cs:35-36); they are used only in the non-buffered branch (61-67). The interceptor creates one handler per request (MetricsInterceptor.cs:36-43). MonitorHandler has the same eager pair (MonitorHandler.cs:31-32) but only while capturing.

**Failure scenario.** A production client with metrics enabled pays three heap objects (~180 bytes on 64-bit) per request on top of the pipeline, also for buffered responses and failed requests that never use the delegates.

## Suggested fix
Create the delegates lazily in the streaming branch, or let ObservedResponseBodySource call back through an interface implemented by the handler so no delegate is needed.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Delegates are created only in the streaming branch (or replaced by an interface callback), so a buffered response allocates only the handler.
- [ ] Allocation per buffered request through MetricsInterceptor is reduced by the two delegates, measured and stated in the PR.
