title: [Observability] MetricsHandler and MonitorInterceptor read the disposed UHttpRequest when a streamed body is disposed, so disposal throws ObjectDisposedException
body:
## Summary
For a client-owned request, UHttpRequest.SendStreamingAsync disposes the request as soon as headers arrive, and later Content or TryGetBufferedContent calls throw. MetricsHandler and MonitorInterceptor read the request in the body-dispose callback, so awaiting DisposeAsync of any streamed response throws and the completion is never recorded. The Monitor silently shows no entry. FileDownloader fails after the file is committed whenever a MetricsInterceptor is present.

## Location
- `Runtime/Observability/MetricsHandler.cs:101`

## Problem
UHttpRequest.SendStreamingAsync (Runtime/Core/UHttpRequest.cs:390-405) calls Dispose() in its finally as soon as headers arrive; for a client-owned request that sets _disposeRequested, and ThrowIfDisposed (UHttpRequest.cs:564-575) then throws for every later call of the Content getter (:49-55) and TryGetBufferedContent (:70-72), even though the lease is still held by the response. For a streamed body MetricsHandler defers completion to ObservedResponseBodySource's dispose callback (MetricsHandler.cs:61-67, 120-123); CompleteResponse sets _completionRecorded, reads RequestBodyBytesSent (0 for a body-less request) and then evaluates `_request.Content.Length` (MetricsHandler.cs:96-104) -> ObjectDisposedException before Successful/FailedRequests and RecordCompletion run. The callback runs in the finally of ObservedResponseBodySource.DisposeAsync (ObservedResponseBodySource.cs:141-159), so the exception escapes through UHttpStreamingResponse.DisposeAsyncCore (Runtime/Core/UHttpStreamingResponse.cs:227-237) to the caller (the sync Dispose path swallows it in AbortAfterFailedBodyDispose). MonitorInterceptor.BuildMonitorEvent hits the same guard at MonitorInterceptor.cs:350 (`request.TryGetBufferedContent`); Capture's catch (MonitorInterceptor.cs:317-334) turns it into LogCaptureFailure, which is silent because nothing in the package sets DiagnosticLogger (MonitorInterceptor.cs:907-911). HTTP/1.1 bodies never expose buffered data (Http11ResponseBodySource.TryGetBufferedData returns false), so every real streamed response takes this path. All tests in Tests/Runtime/Observability and UHttpClientStreamingContextLifetimeTests use `new UHttpRequest(...)` (not client-owned, guard never trips), so nothing covers it.

**Failure scenario.** Client with a MetricsInterceptor; the documented pattern `await using var s = await client.Get(url).SendStreamingAsync(ct);` (Documentation~/Modules/Core.md:100) or FileDownloader.DownloadFileAsync (FileDownloader.cs:399 uses the fluent send, :370-374 disposes in finally). At the end of the block DisposeAsync throws ObjectDisposedException(UHttpRequest): FileDownloader has already committed the file but the call fails; SuccessfulRequests/FailedRequests and the average are never updated for any streamed GET. In the Editor the HTTP Monitor silently shows no entry for any streamed request sent through the fluent API.

## Suggested fix
Snapshot what the handlers need (content length / buffered request body reference / capture note) while the request is live (in the interceptor lambda or OnRequestStart) instead of touching the UHttpRequest in the dispose callback; make observer dispose callbacks non-throwing (catch in InvokeDisposeCallback). Add tests that send a client-created request with request.SendStreamingAsync() through Metrics and Monitor.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] MetricsHandler and MonitorInterceptor snapshot the request data they need (content length, buffered request body, capture note) while the request is live and never touch UHttpRequest in the dispose callback.
- [ ] Observer dispose callbacks cannot throw out of ObservedResponseBodySource.DisposeAsync.
- [ ] Successful/FailedRequests and the Monitor event are recorded for a streamed response from a client-created request sent with request.SendStreamingAsync().
- [ ] Deterministic NUnit regression test in Tests/Runtime/Observability/ using a client-owned request through Metrics and Monitor, failing before the fix.

UHttpClient passes the client-owned request unchanged into the pipeline (UHttpClient.cs:471-473) and Metrics is canonically outermost (Documentation~/Modules/Interceptors.md:55), so MetricsHandler._request is that object (MetricsInterceptor.cs:36-43). The callback runs in the finally of ObservedResponseBodySource.DisposeAsync (155-158) and escapes UHttpStreamingResponse.DisposeAsyncCore (UHttpStreamingResponse.cs:227-237). title: [Observability] HttpMetrics.RequestsByHost grows without bound, one entry per distinct host requested
body:
## Summary
MetricsInterceptor adds every request host to a ConcurrentDictionary that is only cleared by Reset(). When the interceptor sits inside the redirect interceptor, every redirect hop host chosen by the peer becomes a key. Long-running clients using per-user or generated hostnames accumulate entries for the client lifetime.

## Location
- `Runtime/Observability/MetricsInterceptor.cs:34`

## Problem
Each dispatch runs `_metrics.RequestsByHost.AddOrUpdate(request.Uri.Host, 1, ...)` (MetricsInterceptor.cs:34) on a ConcurrentDictionary<string, long> (HttpMetrics.cs:42-43) that is only cleared by Reset(). When the interceptor sits inside the redirect interceptor the host of every redirect hop, which the peer chooses, becomes a key.

**Failure scenario.** A long-running client that talks to per-user or per-shard hostnames, or follows redirects to generated CDN hostnames, accumulates one dictionary node and one host string per name for the lifetime of the client.

## Suggested fix
Cap the number of tracked hosts (count the rest under an 'other' key) or make per-host tracking opt-in.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The number of tracked hosts is capped (remaining hosts counted under an 'other' key) or per-host tracking is opt-in; the cap is documented.
- [ ] Memory held by RequestsByHost is bounded regardless of the number of distinct hosts.

## Summary
MonitorHandler copies chunks into a SegmentedBuffer up to the text capture limit unless the content type is on a fixed binary list, and the NUL-byte sniff runs only when the event is built. Binary bodies are cut to 64 KB afterwards, and in-flight buffers are not counted against MaxTotalCaptureBytes. Parallel downloads with missing or unlisted content types can hold hundreds of megabytes in the Editor.

## Location
- `Runtime/Observability/MonitorHandler.cs:106`

## Problem
OnResponseStartAsync sets `_bufferedCaptureLimit = GetBufferedResponseCaptureLimit(headers)` (MonitorHandler.cs:49), which is the 64 KB binary preview only for a fixed list of content types and otherwise max(MaxCaptureSizeBytes, BinaryPreviewBytes) capped by a quarter of the budget (MonitorInterceptor.cs:582-589, 605-633). CaptureBody copies every chunk into a SegmentedBuffer up to that limit (MonitorHandler.cs:106-117). The NUL-byte sniff runs only when the event is built (MonitorInterceptor.cs:549-555), where a binary body is cut down to 64 KB. MaxTotalCaptureBytes accounts stored events only (StoreEvent, 747-774).

**Failure scenario.** Editor Play Mode with the Monitor open and 40 parallel downloads whose Content-Type is missing or not in the list (binary/octet-stream, model/gltf-binary, application/x-gzip): 40 x 5 MB = 200 MB of pooled segments are filled and copied, then all but 64 KB of each is thrown away.

## Suggested fix
Sniff the first chunk (the first 512 bytes) and lower the limit to BinaryPreviewBytes immediately when it looks binary; optionally count in-flight capture bytes against the budget.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The first chunk (first 512 bytes) is sniffed and the capture limit drops to the binary preview size immediately when the body looks binary.
- [ ] In-flight capture bytes are bounded (counted against the budget or capped).
- [ ] Deterministic NUnit test in Tests/Runtime/Observability/ streaming a binary body without a listed content type and asserting captured bytes stay at or below the preview limit.

title: [Observability] MonitorInterceptor.DiagnosticLogger is never assigned so capture failures are dropped; HeaderValueTransform duplicates RedactionPolicy
body:
## Summary
LogCaptureFailure returns silently because nothing sets MonitorInterceptor.DiagnosticLogger, so a throwing subscriber or event builder yields an empty Monitor and no log output. HeaderValueTransform is an untested second redaction hook beside RedactionPolicy. The cooldown and suppression logic therefore never produces output.

## Location
- `Runtime/Observability/MonitorInterceptor.cs:94`

## Problem
LogCaptureFailure (MonitorInterceptor.cs:869-921) throttles and formats a message, then returns at 907-911 when DiagnosticLogger is null. rg shows no assignment of MonitorInterceptor.DiagnosticLogger in Editor/, Runtime/, Samples~, Documentation~ or Tests (TurboHttpSettings.ApplyMonitorPreferences, lines 135-147, sets every other static but this one), although Observability can reach Core's TurboDiagnostics. HeaderValueTransform (77-87, applied at 447-457) is described as 'for example redaction', is not referenced by any test, document or Editor code, and overlaps RedactionPolicy.

**Failure scenario.** A subscriber to OnRequestCaptured or the event builder throws on every request: the Monitor shows nothing and nothing is logged, and the 50 lines of cooldown/suppression logic never produce output.

## Suggested fix
Route capture failures to TurboDiagnostics by default (type names only) or have TurboHttpSettings install Debug.LogWarning; remove HeaderValueTransform or cover it with a test and document its ordering relative to the policy.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Capture failures are routed to TurboDiagnostics by default, logging type names only and no sensitive data.
- [ ] HeaderValueTransform is removed, or covered by a test and documented with its order relative to RedactionPolicy.
- [ ] Deterministic NUnit test in Tests/Runtime/Observability/ where a subscriber throws and the failure reaches the diagnostic sink.

title: [Observability] MonitorInterceptor is a 943-line all-static type with dead overloads, a duplicated binary content-type table and a stale comment
body:
## Summary
All Monitor state is static, so two clients cannot have different capture settings and tests must restore globals. The type mixes configuration, ring-buffer storage, event building, binary detection and log throttling, and contains unused overloads, a no-op CloneBody and two copies of the same content-type table. A comment claims HttpHeaders yields only the first value per name, which is wrong.

## Location
- `Runtime/Observability/MonitorInterceptor.cs:285`

## Problem
The instance has no fields; all state is static (MonitorInterceptor.cs:29-45), so two clients cannot have different capture settings and tests must restore globals. Dead code: the 6-argument Capture overload (285-305; MonitorHandler.cs:142-150 calls only the 8-argument one and Observability grants no InternalsVisibleTo), CreateBodySnapshot(byte[], ...) (465-475) and CreateBodySnapshot(ReadOnlySequence, headers) (515-523); HttpMonitorEvent.CloneBody is a no-op (HttpMonitorEvent.cs:271-276). HasClearlyBinaryContentType (MonitorInterceptor.cs:605-633) and HasLikelyBinaryContentType (HttpMonitorEvent.cs:235-269) are two copies of the same 15-entry table, and the 512-byte sample size exists as BinaryDetectionSampleBytes (26) and as a literal (HttpMonitorEvent.cs:194). The comment at 419-420 says the HttpHeaders enumerator 'only yields the first value per name', but Runtime/Core/HttpHeaders.cs:139-148 yields one item per value.

**Failure scenario.** A content type added to one binary table (for example application/wasm) makes the buffered capture limit and the stored/preview classification disagree for the same response; readers following the stale comment avoid the enumerator for no reason.

## Suggested fix
Split storage (history ring + budget), event construction and configuration into separate internal types, keep one content-type classifier, and delete the unused overloads and the stale comment.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Storage, event construction and configuration are split into separate internal types, with one shared binary content-type classifier and one sample-size constant.
- [ ] The unused Capture and CreateBodySnapshot overloads, the no-op CloneBody and the stale comment are removed.
- [ ] Existing Observability tests pass and a new test in Tests/Runtime/Observability/ asserts the capture limit and the stored classification agree for a content type such as application/wasm.

title: [Observability] Editor Monitor captures, displays and exports request and response bodies without redaction
body:
## Summary
BuildMonitorEvent snapshots up to 5 MB of the buffered request body and the response body as raw bytes. The Monitor window shows them and Export writes them as text and base64 into files the export code describes as safe to share. RedactionPolicy has no body hook, while RecordReplay already redacts JSON and form fields. Passwords and access tokens in login bodies end up in exported JSON.

## Location
- `Runtime/Observability/MonitorInterceptor.cs:349`

## Problem
BuildMonitorEvent snapshots up to MaxCaptureSizeBytes (5 MB) of the buffered request body and the response body as raw bytes (349-365); the window shows them (HttpMonitorWindow.Panels.cs:251,285) and ExportEvent writes them as text and base64 (HttpMonitorWindow.Export.cs:146-162). RedactionPolicy has no body hook. RecordReplay already redacts JSON/form fields; the Monitor does not.

**Failure scenario.** A login POST with password=.. or a token response {"access_token":..} is held in the history and written in clear to an exported http_event_*.json that the export code comments describe as safe to share.

## Suggested fix
Tracked by #117 (body redaction delegate, fail closed). Until then reuse the RecordReplay JSON/form field redaction for text bodies at capture or at least at export.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Text request and response bodies are redacted at capture or at least at export, reusing the RecordReplay JSON/form field redaction, with fail-closed behaviour when redaction cannot run.
- [ ] Exported http_event_*.json contains no unredacted secret fields from a login POST or token response.
- [ ] Deterministic NUnit regression test in Tests/Runtime/Observability/ with a password form body and an access_token JSON body, failing before the fix.

## Context

title: [Observability] Monitor timeline data and error text bypass RedactionPolicy, leaking full URLs with raw query strings
body:
## Summary
BuildMonitorEvent redacts only the request URI and header values. Timeline values (redirect from/to, cache key/uri) and error text are copied with ToString(), so URLs with user-info and query secrets reach the Monitor Timeline tab, the Export JSON and LoggingHandler.LogError output. With default settings (Redact Captured Secrets on) an access_token query value shows as redacted in the list but in clear in the timeline and export.

## Location
- `Runtime/Observability/MonitorInterceptor.cs:661`

## Problem
BuildMonitorEvent redacts only request.Uri and header values (MonitorInterceptor.cs:348,360,376). CopyTimeline/CopyTimelineData (635-676) copy every timeline value with ToString() and no policy. The values are peer/request URLs: RedirectHandler.cs:230-236 records { from = _currentRequest.Uri.AbsoluteUri, to = targetUri.AbsoluteUri } (user-info and query included); CacheInterceptor.cs:344-386,423 and CacheInterceptor.StreamingDispatch.cs:22 record key/uri = method + NormalizeUri(uri), which keeps the raw query (CacheInterceptor.UriNormalization.cs:16-42). The Editor shows them (HttpMonitorWindow.Panels.cs:324-327) and Export writes them unredacted (HttpMonitorWindow.Export.cs:192-217) although the same export re-redacts URL and headers 'to prevent credential leakage when files are shared' (Export.cs:131-132). Error text has the same hole: ResolveError stores HttpError.ToString() (MonitorInterceptor.cs:699-706), Export writes evt.Error (Export.cs:102) and LoggingHandler.LogError logs error.Message at every log level (LoggingHandler.cs:229), while RedirectHandler.cs:186,198 embed full URLs in those messages. No test covers timeline or error redaction (Tests/Runtime/Observability only asserts Timeline[0].Data["attempt"]).

**Failure scenario.** Default settings (Redact Captured Secrets on). A client with CacheInterceptor requests https://api.example.com/items?access_token=SECRET. The Monitor list shows access_token=[REDACTED], but the Timeline tab shows 'CacheMiss key = GET https://api.example.com/items?access_token=SECRET', and the exported JSON contains it. A 302 chain adds 'Redirect from/to' with the raw query of every hop; a blocked downgrade logs 'Blocked insecure redirect downgrade from https://...?token=SECRET' through LoggingInterceptor at Minimal level.

## Suggested fix
Run timeline values and error strings through the active RedactionPolicy at capture time (RedactUrl for values that parse as absolute URLs, or redact by known keys from/to/key/uri) and again in Export; redact or drop URLs from error.Message in LoggingHandler. #117 names 'exceptions/timeline' as future scope but ships v1.0 with this default-path leak; the point fix belongs with #92/#65.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Timeline values and error strings are passed through the active RedactionPolicy at capture time and again at Export (URL values redacted).
- [ ] LoggingHandler.LogError no longer logs unredacted URLs from error.Message.
- [ ] Deterministic NUnit regression test in Tests/Runtime/Observability/ with a cache miss and a redirect carrying ?access_token=SECRET, asserting the secret is absent from timeline, error text and export, failing before the fix.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `util-protocol-01` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/util.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: security.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. MonitorInterceptor.BuildMonitorEvent applies the policy only to request.Uri and header values (MonitorInterceptor.cs:348,360,376); CopyTimeline/CopyTimelineData/ConvertTimelineValue (635-693) copy every value with ToString() and no policy. Sources of URL values: RedirectHandler.cs:230-236 records from/to = Uri.AbsoluteUri (query and user-info included) on the shared RequestContext, so the next hop's Monitor event carries them; CacheInterceptor.cs:344-386 records key = BuildBaseKey = method + NormalizeUri (CacheInterceptor.Variants.cs:105-108, query kept at UriNormalization.cs:29-40). The window prints them (HttpMonitorWindow.Panels.cs:324-327) and Export writes them raw (Export.cs:192-217) while URL/headers are re-redacted (Export.cs:96,131-135). Error text: LoggingHandler.LogError appends error.Message at any non-None level (LoggingHandler.cs:215-231; UHttpException.Message = UHttpError.Message) and RedirectHandler.cs:186,198 embed full URLs. One correction: the auto-appended Monitor is innermost (UHttpClient.cs:822), so it does not receive redirect-generated errors; the Monitor error-text leak needs a manually placed monitor, the timeline leak does not. Only test touching timeline is MonitorInterceptorTests.cs:80-82. #117 Step 1 names 'exceptions/timeline' as scope (v1.1), so tracked.

Related: #117, [[R11-util-protocol-03]], [[R11-util-protocol-12]].

title: [Packaging] ObservabilityModuleRegistration is a [Preserve]d RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod compiled into players, rooting the Editor-only HTTP Monitor
body:
## Summary
The registration method has no UNITY_EDITOR guard, but its only consumer, EditorMonitorHook.TryAppend, is called under UNITY_EDITOR in UHttpClient. In a player the factory is registered at startup and never read, yet the linker roots MonitorInterceptor and everything it reaches (about 1,900 lines). This costs build size and startup time in every player that includes the assembly.

## Location
- `Runtime/Observability/ObservabilityModuleRegistration.cs:23`

## Problem
ObservabilityModuleRegistration.cs:23-28 marks EnsureRegistered with [Preserve] and [RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod(SubsystemRegistration)] with no #if UNITY_EDITOR; it registers CreateMonitorInterceptor (30-45), which references MonitorInterceptor.CaptureEnabled and new MonitorInterceptor(). The only consumer, EditorMonitorHook.TryAppend, is called from Runtime/Core/UHttpClient.cs:794-796 and 801-823 inside #if UNITY_EDITOR, so in a player the registered factory is never invoked. UnityLinker roots methods carrying RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod/[Preserve] at every stripping level, so everything reachable from the factory stays: MonitorInterceptor.cs (943 lines), MonitorHandler.cs (163), HttpMonitorEvent.cs (312), ObservedResponseBodySource.cs (199), RedactionPolicy.cs (239), plus Core's EditorMonitorHook (58) and their generic instantiations (ReadOnlyDictionary<string,string>, ValueTuple<string,UHttpErrorType?,HttpMonitorFailureKind>, List<HttpMonitorTimelineEvent>...). TurboHTTP.Observability.asmdef is autoReferenced with no platform or define constraint, so the assembly is always in the linker input. A side effect of the hook design is that the pipeline a client runs differs between Editor play mode (extra innermost interceptor appended by Core) and players.

**Failure scenario.** A project that uses only Core + Transport (never references TurboHTTP.Observability) builds an IL2CPP player with Managed Stripping High: about 1,900 source lines of Editor monitor code and the startup registration call are still compiled into the player, and the registration runs at every player start for a hook nothing reads.

## Suggested fix
Compile the registration (and the [Preserve]/RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod attributes) only under UNITY_EDITOR, or move the registration into TurboHTTP.Editor through a narrow Core entry point. Keep MonitorInterceptor usable in players only when application code references it explicitly.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The registration and its [Preserve]/RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod attributes compile only under UNITY_EDITOR, or move behind a narrow Core entry point in TurboHTTP.Editor.
- [ ] MonitorInterceptor remains usable in players when application code references it explicitly.
- [ ] Editor behaviour is unchanged: the auto-appended Monitor still works in Play Mode, covered by an NUnit test in Tests/Runtime/Observability/.
- [ ] Stripping effect checked in a player build and recorded, or marked as not run.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `util-design-01` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/util.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: pluggability.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Runtime/Observability/ObservabilityModuleRegistration.cs:23-28 has [Preserve] + [RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod(SubsystemRegistration)] with no UNITY_EDITOR guard (rg finds no UNITY_EDITOR in Runtime/Observability) and registers a factory that constructs MonitorInterceptor (30-45). The only reader, EditorMonitorHook.TryAppend, is called solely from Runtime/Core/UHttpClient.cs:794-796/801-823 inside #if UNITY_EDITOR (rg EditorMonitorHook: no other runtime caller). TurboHTTP.Observability.asmdef has no platform or define constraint. So in a player the method runs at startup for a hook nothing reads and roots MonitorInterceptor and what it reaches. That UnityLinker treats these attributes as roots is Unity's documented behaviour, not measured here (no player build run). The mechanism came from #186 (closed), which did not consider the player side. Build-size and startup cost only, no functional defect.

Related: #258.

title: [Observability] 'Enable HTTP Monitor' is evaluated at client construction, so enabling it during play has no effect on existing clients
body:
## Summary
CreateMonitorInterceptor returns null when CaptureEnabled is false, and it runs once per UHttpClient construction. The interceptor already checks IsCapturing per request and is a pass-through when off. A developer who enables the Monitor after the game created a long-lived client sees nothing until play mode restarts.

## Location
- `Runtime/Observability/ObservabilityModuleRegistration.cs:32`

## Problem
CreateMonitorInterceptor returns null when MonitorInterceptor.CaptureEnabled is false (ObservabilityModuleRegistration.cs:32-33); it runs once per UHttpClient construction (UHttpClient.cs:794-822). The interceptor itself already checks IsCapturing per request and is a pass-through when it is false (MonitorInterceptor.cs:272-275), so the construction-time check only prevents later activation. TurboHttpSettings.cs:137 sets CaptureEnabled from the preference at any time.

**Failure scenario.** Monitor is disabled in Preferences, the game starts and creates its long-lived client, the developer enables the Monitor and opens the window: nothing is captured until play mode is restarted.

## Suggested fix
Always append the interceptor in the Editor (it adds no per-request work while IsCapturing is false) and let CaptureEnabled act only per request.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] In the Editor the Monitor interceptor is always appended and CaptureEnabled is checked per request only.
- [ ] With capture off the interceptor adds no per-request work beyond the check.
- [ ] Deterministic NUnit test in Tests/Runtime/Observability/ that creates a client with capture disabled, enables it, and asserts the next request is captured.

title: [Observability] ObservedResponseBodySource runs chunk and dispose callbacks without mutual exclusion, writing into returned pooled buffers
body:
## Summary
ReadAsync invokes the chunk callback after the await without checking disposal, while DisposeAsync invokes the dispose callback on another thread. MonitorHandler and LoggingHandler share unsynchronised fields and pooled buffers between the two, so a late chunk can write into an ArrayPool segment already returned and reused, or rent a buffer that is never returned. The verifier found the trigger narrower than reported but the missing exclusion is real.

## Location
- `Runtime/Observability/ObservedResponseBodySource.cs:87`

## Problem
ReadAsync awaits the inner read and then calls `_onChunkRead` (ObservedResponseBodySource.cs:79-88) without re-checking _disposed; DisposeAsync (141-159) sets _disposed, disposes the inner source and calls `_onDispose` on the disposing thread. Core does not serialise Dispose against an in-flight read (UHttpStreamingResponse.Dispose/DisposeAsync, Runtime/Core/UHttpStreamingResponse.cs:89-118; ResponseBodyStream only checks a flag before the read starts). MonitorHandler.CaptureBody writes `_responseBody` (SegmentedBuffer of pooled 16 KB segments) and plain int/long fields (MonitorHandler.cs:98-122) while CaptureOnce reads AsSequence(), disposes the buffer and zeroes the same fields from the other thread (132-160); none of these fields is volatile or locked. LoggingHandler.CaptureBodyPreview copies into `_bodyPreview` (LoggingHandler.cs:168-191) while CompleteLogging -> ReturnBodyPreviewBuffer returns that array to ByteArrayPool and nulls the field (193-213, 242-251); a callback arriving after completion rents a new 500-byte array (line 177) that nothing returns because _completionLogged is already 1.

**Failure scenario.** Main thread disposes a streaming response (scene teardown, user cancel) while a thread-pool read of the same body completes with data. Monitor (Editor window open or CaptureWithoutViewer): CaptureBody writes captured bytes into a SegmentedBuffer segment that CaptureOnce already returned to ArrayPool, which another request may have rented -> bytes of one response appear in another request's buffer; or, on ARM64 where the zeroed _bufferedCaptureLimit is not yet visible, a fresh SegmentedBuffer is created after capture and its segments are never returned. Logging at Detailed+logBody: up to 500 bytes written into a returned pooled array, or a rented preview buffer leaked (ByteArrayPool ActiveCount drifts).

## Suggested fix
Give the observation one owner: guard chunk and dispose callbacks with a small lock/state in ObservedResponseBodySource (skip `_onChunkRead` once disposal has started and let the dispose callback wait for an in-flight chunk callback), or lock inside MonitorHandler/LoggingHandler around buffer access and completion.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Chunk and dispose callbacks are serialised (a lock or state in ObservedResponseBodySource, or locking in the handlers); chunk callbacks are skipped once disposal starts.
- [ ] Pooled capture and preview buffers are returned exactly once and never written after return, including on late chunk completion.
- [ ] Deterministic NUnit regression test in Tests/Runtime/Observability/ that completes a read concurrently with dispose and asserts no write after return and ByteArrayPool ActiveCount returns to its baseline.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `util-runtime-02` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/util.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: concurrency.

Verification: Plausible: the code is as described; the outcome depends on runtime, device or peer behaviour that a static review cannot settle.

Verifier note: The missing mutual exclusion is real: ReadAsync invokes _onChunkRead after the await without re-checking _disposed (ObservedResponseBodySource.cs:79-88) and DisposeAsync invokes _onDispose on the disposing thread (141-159); MonitorHandler.CaptureBody/CaptureOnce (MonitorHandler.cs:98-161) and LoggingHandler.CaptureBodyPreview/ReturnBodyPreviewBuffer (LoggingHandler.cs:168-191,242-251) share unsynchronised fields and pooled buffers, and ResponseBodyStream does not serialise reads against dispose (ResponseBodyStream.cs:137-160). But the stated trigger is narrower than claimed: a sync Dispose() of a response whose body has not reached EOF only calls _bodySource.Abort() (UHttpStreamingResponse.cs:155-161) and ObservedResponseBodySource.Abort never invokes the dispose callback (117-123), so the 'main thread disposes during scene teardown' case does not reach CaptureOnce/CompleteLogging at all. The race needs DisposeAsync called from a different flow than the reader while a read completes with data, inside the window of one chunk copy; outcome is timing-dependent and cannot be settled statically.

Related: [[R11-util-runtime-01]].

title: [Observability] PoolHealthReporter.Register<T> is internal with no caller, leaving the ObjectPool reporting path dead and the type untested

title: [Observability] PooledBuffer<T> is public with no user, preserves StackTrace/StackFrame in link.xml and throws NullReferenceException after Dispose in release builds
body:
## Summary
Nothing in the repository uses PooledBuffer<T>, yet Observability link.xml preserves System.Diagnostics.StackTrace and StackFrame for it in every build. Outside DEBUG the Memory getter dereferences a null owner after Dispose, contradicting the XML doc, and DEBUG builds capture a stack trace per instance. The type adds size and a latent defect without a consumer.

## Location
- `Runtime/Observability/PooledBuffer.cs:37`

## Problem
rg over Runtime, Editor, Samples~, Tests and Documentation~ finds no reference to PooledBuffer<T> other than a doc comment in PoolHealthReporter.cs:35. Runtime/Observability/link.xml:9-12 preserves System.Diagnostics.StackTrace and StackFrame with preserve=all for it, and TurboHttpLinkerProcessor merges that file whenever the Observability DLL is in the linker input (always). PooledBuffer.cs:77-90: outside DEBUG/TURBOHTTP_POOL_DIAGNOSTICS the getter does owner.Memory.Slice with owner == null after Dispose, although the XML doc promises ObjectDisposedException only 'in debug builds' and 'pass-through' otherwise. Line 69 captures new StackTrace(1, true).ToString() per instance whenever DEBUG is defined, which includes the Editor and development players.

**Failure scenario.** Every player build carries the StackTrace/StackFrame preserve for a type nothing constructs; a consumer that did adopt it gets a NullReferenceException on use-after-dispose in release builds and a stack-trace capture per rental in development builds.

## Suggested fix
Delete the type and the link.xml rule, or make it internal test support. If it stays public, throw ObjectDisposedException in all configurations and gate the stack capture on TURBOHTTP_POOL_DIAGNOSTICS only.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] PooledBuffer<T> and its link.xml rule are deleted or made internal test support; if kept public, Memory throws ObjectDisposedException in all configurations.
- [ ] Stack capture is gated on TURBOHTTP_POOL_DIAGNOSTICS only.
- [ ] NUnit test in Tests/Runtime/Observability/ asserting use-after-dispose behaviour in the non-debug configuration (if the type stays).

title: [Observability] PooledBuffer<T> captures a full StackTrace with file info on every construction under DEBUG
body:
## Summary
Under `#if DEBUG || TURBOHTTP_POOL_DIAGNOSTICS` the PooledBuffer<T> constructor builds `new StackTrace(skipFrames: 1, fNeedFileInfo: true).ToString()`. Unity defines DEBUG in the Editor and Development builds, so the cost is paid exactly where users profile. Applications that wrap per-message buffers in PooledBuffer pay hundreds of microseconds and several KB of garbage per rent.

## Location
- `Runtime/Observability/PooledBuffer.cs:69`

## Problem
Under `#if DEBUG || TURBOHTTP_POOL_DIAGNOSTICS` the constructor runs `new StackTrace(skipFrames: 1, fNeedFileInfo: true).ToString()` (PooledBuffer.cs:63-70). ## Suggested fix
Gate the stack capture on TURBOHTTP_POOL_DIAGNOSTICS only (keep the cheap double-dispose check under DEBUG), or capture the StackTrace object lazily and format it only when a violation is reported.

title: [Observability] URL-valued headers (Location, Content-Location, Referer, Link) are never query-redacted in logs, Monitor captures, exports or recordings
body:
## Summary
RedactionPolicy.RedactHeaderValue only redacts by header name, and RedactUrl is applied to the request URI only. A 302 Location carrying an OAuth code or a presigned URL signature is stored and printed verbatim by the Monitor, LoggingInterceptor and RecordReplayTransport. The follow-up request URL is redacted while the Location header of the previous hop is not.

## Location
- `Runtime/Observability/RedactionPolicy.cs:134`

## Problem
RedactionPolicy.RedactHeaderValue (134-137) only replaces the value when the header NAME is in the sensitive list; RedactUrl is applied to the request URI only (MonitorInterceptor.cs:376, LoggingInterceptor.cs:74). MonitorInterceptor.CopyHeaders (445), LoggingInterceptor.FormatResponseHeaders (150-153) and RecordReplayTransport.ToDictionary (RecordReplayTransport.Redaction.cs:25-31) therefore store/print a Location value verbatim. The Monitor is appended innermost (UHttpClient.cs:822) and RecordReplay is the transport, so both see every 3xx hop. rg for Location/Referer in Tests/Runtime/Observability, Tests/Runtime/Testing and Tests/Editor returns nothing.

**Failure scenario.** An OAuth authorization-code or download flow answers 302 with 'Location: https://app.example.com/cb?code=AUTHCODE&state=..' or a presigned 'Location: https://bucket.s3.amazonaws.com/obj?X-Amz-Signature=..&X-Amz-Security-Token=..'. The Monitor event for that hop, its exported JSON and a RecordReplay recording committed to the repository contain the code/signature in the Location response header, while the follow-up request's own URL is shown as [REDACTED].

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 10.2.2

## Suggested fix
Treat a small set of URL-valued fields (Location, Content-Location, Referer, Link, Refresh) as URLs in all three sinks: apply RedactUrl (Observability) / NormalizeQuery redaction (RecordReplay) to their values instead of name-only matching, and add a test with a 302 carrying a secret query.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Location, Content-Location, Referer, Link and Refresh values have their query secrets redacted with the URL redaction rules in LoggingInterceptor, MonitorInterceptor (capture and export) and RecordReplayTransport
- [ ] A 302 response with Location carrying code= or X-Amz-Signature= shows the redacted value in all three sinks

title: [Observability] RedactUrl keeps the URI fragment and key-less query components verbatim
body:
## Summary
RedactUrl splits off the fragment and appends it unchanged, and AppendRedactedQuery treats a query pair without '=' as a parameter name and keeps it. A URL such as https://app.example.com/cb#access_token=SECRET or https://cdn.example.com/file?SIGNEDTOKEN is logged and captured with the secret intact under the default policy.

## Location
- `Runtime/Observability/RedactionPolicy.cs:163`

## Problem
RedactUrl splits off '#...' and appends it unchanged (163-165, 179). AppendRedactedQuery treats a pair without '=' as a name and appends it unchanged (219-223). Uri.AbsoluteUri, the input at 151, includes the fragment.

**Failure scenario.** A request URI such as https://app.example.com/cb#access_token=SECRET (OAuth implicit-flow style value passed through by application code) or https://cdn.example.com/file?SIGNEDTOKEN is logged and captured with the secret intact under the default policy.

## Spec reference
RFC 3986 3.5

Redact fragment contents the same way as the query (keep names, drop values, or drop the fragment entirely since it is never sent), and redact a single key-less query component instead of treating it as a parameter name.

title: [Core] The public API for Core's diagnostic sink lives in the optional Observability assembly (TurboHttpDiagnostics)
body:
## Summary
TurboHttpDiagnostics in Observability is a two-method facade over Core's internal TurboDiagnostics.SetSink/ResetSink. The feature is documented as a Core feature, but a project that does not reference Observability cannot silence or route Core's warnings, which the default sink writes to the player log.

## Location
- `Runtime/Observability/TurboHttpDiagnostics.cs:17`

## Problem
TurboHttpDiagnostics.cs:17-37 is a two-method facade over Core's internal TurboDiagnostics.SetSink/ResetSink (Runtime/Core/Internal/TurboDiagnostics.cs:38-49, reachable only through InternalsVisibleTo). The feature is documented as a Core feature (Documentation~/Modules/Core.md:36-46: 'Replace or silence the sink with TurboHTTP.Observability.TurboHttpDiagnostics.SetSink') and its test sits in Tests/Runtime/Core/DiagnosticSinkTests.cs:119-123. The default sink writes Unity console warnings in players.

**Failure scenario.** A size-minded project deletes or does not reference TurboHTTP.Observability (an 'independently includable feature module' per architecture.md): it has no way to stop Core from writing warnings to the player log or to send them to its own logger, because the setter is internal to Core.

## Suggested fix
Expose the sink setter from Core (a small public static in TurboHTTP.Core) and keep the Observability type as a forwarding alias or obsolete it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A public static SetSink/ResetSink API exists in TurboHTTP.Core and Documentation~/Modules/Core.md references it
- [ ] The Observability type forwards to the Core API or is marked obsolete
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Testing] MockHttpServer.When publishes the route before it is configured and the builder mutates it without the server lock
body:
## Summary
MockHttpServer.When adds the route with a default 200 handler to _routes under the lock and returns a builder whose Priority, Times, WithHeader, WithBody and Respond write the live route without locking. User matchers are invoked while holding _lock. Adding a route during in-flight requests can match a half-built route or read Matchers while it is appended, and a blocking matcher stalls all dispatch.

## Location
- `Runtime/Testing/MockHttpServer.cs:55`

## Problem
When (MockHttpServer.cs:40-62) adds the route with a default '200 empty' handler and no matchers to _routes under _lock, then returns a builder whose Priority/Times/WithHeader/WithBody/Respond (449-545) write _route.Priority, RemainingInvocations, Handler and Matchers (a List<T>) with no lock or volatile. TryMatchRoute iterates route.Matchers and invokes each user delegate while holding _lock (274-309).

**Failure scenario.** A route is added while requests are in flight (a common pattern for 'next call fails' tests): a concurrent request can match the half-built route and receive the default 200, or read Matchers while the builder appends to it; a matcher that blocks stalls every other dispatch and RecordHistory.

## Suggested fix
Build the route in the builder and publish it atomically on Respond (or an explicit Register), copying matchers into an immutable array; evaluate matchers on a snapshot outside the lock.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The route is built by the builder and published atomically on Respond, with matchers copied to an immutable array
- [ ] Matchers are evaluated outside the server lock on a snapshot
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Testing/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Testing] MockHttpServer.DispatchAsync awaits the handler and response delay without ConfigureAwait(false)
body:
## Summary
The awaits on route.Handler and Task.Delay in MockHttpServer.DispatchAsync are the only ones in the utility modules without ConfigureAwait(false). A request started on the Unity main thread captures UnitySynchronizationContext, so a test that blocks the main thread while waiting for a delayed mock response deadlocks. This violates the platform.md rule that library code never relies on the caller's SynchronizationContext.

## Location
- `Runtime/Testing/MockHttpServer.cs:163`

## Problem
`responseModel = await route.Handler(mockContext);` (MockHttpServer.cs:157) and `await Task.Delay(responseModel.Delay, cancellationToken);` (163) are the only awaits in the four runtime modules of this slice without ConfigureAwait(false). MockTransport.DispatchAsync calls the server delegate synchronously on the caller's thread (MockTransport.cs:240), so when the request is started on the main thread the UnitySynchronizationContext is captured. platform.md requires library code never to rely on the caller's SynchronizationContext (#245), and testing.md line 39 notes that Unity's context does not pump in tests.

**Failure scenario.** EditMode test on the main thread: `server.When(GET, "/x").Respond(r => r.Delay(TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(10)))` and the test waits on the request with a blocking wait (the usual pattern without async test support in Unity 2021.3's test framework): the Task.Delay continuation is posted to the main thread that is blocked -> the test hangs forever. In PlayMode each delayed or async mock response costs a main-thread hop and the rest of the pipeline (handlers, body collection) then runs on the main thread.

## Suggested fix
Add ConfigureAwait(false) to both awaits.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Both awaits use ConfigureAwait(false)
- [ ] A delayed mock response completes while the starting thread blocks on the request task under a single-threaded SynchronizationContext
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Testing/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `util-runtime-08` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/util.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: platform-compat.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Runtime/Testing/MockHttpServer.cs:157 and 163 are the only single-statement awaits in JSON/Files/Observability/Testing without ConfigureAwait(false) (rg over the four modules; the other hits continue on the next line). MockTransport.DispatchAsync reaches the delegate synchronously (MockTransport.cs:240) and Runtime/Core has no Task.Run/Yield hop on the send path, so a main-thread caller's UnitySynchronizationContext is captured for a Delay or a truly async handler; this breaks the platform.md:38-39 rule (#245). Not a default-path hang: the default route handlers complete synchronously (MockHttpServer.cs:49,532,562), the deadlock needs the caller to block the main thread, and the repo's own guidance runs async helpers through Task.Run (testing.md:39). Testing-module only, hence low.

Also reported as `util-design-25` (merged into this issue).

title: [Testing] MockRouteBuilder.WithJsonBody<T> swallows every exception and turns configuration errors into a 404
body:
## Summary
WithJsonBody<T> wraps ProjectJsonBridge.Deserialize and the user predicate in a bare catch that returns false. A missing JSON bridge, an unsupported POCO type with LiteJson and exceptions thrown by the predicate are hidden, and the request gets the generic 404 'No mock route matched request.' with no hint of the cause.

## Location
- `Runtime/Testing/MockHttpServer.cs:520`

## Problem
MockHttpServer.cs:513-523 wraps ProjectJsonBridge.Deserialize and the user predicate in 'catch { return false; }'. That hides InvalidOperationException 'no JSON bridge is registered' (ProjectJsonBridge.cs:48-54), NotSupportedException from LiteJson for a POCO T (LiteJsonSerializer.cs:300-306), and exceptions thrown by the predicate itself (for example an NUnit assertion). The route then does not match and DispatchAsync answers 404 'No mock route matched request.' (145-153).

**Failure scenario.** A test registers When(POST, "/login").WithJsonBody<LoginDto>(d => d.user == "a") in a project whose default serializer is LiteJson: every request gets a 404 and nothing says that LoginDto cannot be deserialized.

## Suggested fix
Catch only the data-level JsonSerializationException wrapper for 'body is not this JSON', and let configuration errors (no bridge, unsupported type) and predicate exceptions propagate.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Only the data-level JSON deserialization failure means 'body does not match'
- [ ] Missing bridge, unsupported type and predicate exceptions propagate to the test

title: [Testing] Public MockRoute, MockTransport's dummy ctor flag and RecordReplayMismatchPolicy.Warn without an inner transport are unusable or misleading
body:
## Summary
MockRoute is public but no public API accepts or returns one. MockTransport is unsealed with no virtual members and has a discarded `preferValueTaskHandler` constructor flag used only to disambiguate overloads. RecordReplayTransport applies Warn and Relaxed only when an inner transport exists, so replay-only Warn behaves like Strict without logging. The recording enums and option members have no XML docs.

## Location
- `Runtime/Testing/MockRoute.cs:9`

## Problem
MockRoute (MockRoute.cs:9-20) is public with public setters, but no public API returns or accepts one (MockRouteBuilder keeps it private, MockHttpServer.cs:440-447). MockTransport is an unsealed public class with no virtual members (MockTransport.cs:19) and a constructor parameter 'bool preferValueTaskHandler = true' that is discarded (97-104) and exists only to break an overload ambiguity. RecordReplayTransport.TryResolveReplay (RecordReplayTransport.cs:569-578) applies Warn and Relaxed fallbacks only when _innerTransport != null; with a replay-only transport Warn behaves exactly like Strict and does not even log. RecordReplayMode, RecordReplayMismatchPolicy, RecordReplayTransportOptions members and RecordReplayRedactionPolicy members (21-58, 184-194) have no XML docs, so the difference between Warn and Relaxed is discoverable only from the code. MockHistoryEntry and MockResponse are fully mutable (MockRoute.cs:22-66).

**Failure scenario.** A CI suite constructs RecordReplayTransport(null, {Mode=Replay, MismatchPolicy=Warn}) expecting unmatched requests to be reported as warnings: they fail as errors with no log line.

## Suggested fix
Make MockRoute internal, seal MockTransport and replace the flag with distinctly named factory methods, validate Warn/Relaxed against a missing inner transport in the constructor (or log), and document the enums.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] MockRoute is internal and MockTransport is sealed; the dummy flag is replaced by distinctly named factory methods
- [ ] Warn/Relaxed without an inner transport is rejected in the constructor or logged

title: [Testing] MockTransport and RecordReplay Replay ignore request.Timeout and an already-cancelled token
body:
## Summary
RawSocketTransport enforces request.Timeout and maps expiry to UHttpErrorType.Timeout, but MockTransport and Replay mode only pass the caller token to the delay. A pre-cancelled token with no delay still delivers a response. A test that enqueues a 30 s delay with a 1 s timeout passes or hangs where production fails with Timeout, so timeout and retry handling cannot be tested.

## Location
- `Runtime/Testing/MockTransport.cs:201`

## Problem
The error model puts timeouts in the transport: RawSocketTransport applies timeoutCts.CancelAfter(request.Timeout) and maps expiry to UHttpErrorType.Timeout (RawSocketTransport.cs:440, 834-835); nothing in UHttpClient or Core/Pipeline reads request.Timeout. MockTransport.DispatchAsync (201-274) only passes the caller token to Task.Delay(queued.Delay) and to the fallback handler; request.Timeout is used solely to copy the snapshot (379). It also never calls cancellationToken.ThrowIfCancellationRequested(), so a pre-cancelled token with no delay still delivers the response. RecordReplayTransport Replay (396-415) likewise ignores Timeout. Bodies are delivered for HEAD/204/304 unchanged. Documentation~/Modules/Testing.md does not mention any of this.

**Failure scenario.** A test does transport.EnqueueResponse(delay: TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30)) and client.Get(url).WithTimeout(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1)) to verify its timeout/retry handling. With RawSocketTransport the request fails with UHttpErrorType.Timeout after 1 s; with MockTransport it succeeds after 30 s, so the test either hangs or passes while the production path behaves differently.

## Suggested fix
Give the test transports the same deadline semantics as the real one: link a CancelAfter(request.Timeout) source in MockTransport/Replay dispatch and report UHttpErrorType.Timeout through OnResponseError, check the caller token before delivering, and document the remaining differences (no HEAD/204 body suppression, streaming request bodies are not read).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] MockTransport and Replay link a CancelAfter(request.Timeout) source and report UHttpErrorType.Timeout
- [ ] The caller token is checked before delivering a response and cancellation surfaces as cancellation
- [ ] Remaining differences from the real transport are documented in Documentation~/Modules/Testing.md
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Testing/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Core] Transport contract (TransportBehaviorFlags, buffered body source, callback wrapper) is internal, so third parties cannot write a conforming transport
body:
## Summary
MockTransport and RecordReplayTransport rely on internal Core types via InternalsVisibleTo, including TransportBehaviorFlags.SelfDrainsResponseBody, HandlerCallbackSafetyWrapper and BufferedResponseBodySource. architecture.md requires every transport to set that flag, but an external transport can only hard-code the string. Under #76, publish the transport-facing contract (the behavior flags, a buffered body source factory, the callback safety wrapper) and a public request-body extension point.

title: [Testing] MockTransport retains a snapshot of every request including a body copy in an unbounded queue
body:
## Summary
MockTransport.CaptureRequest copies each buffered body and enqueues a new UHttpRequest into _capturedRequests, which is cleared only by ClearCapturedRequests or Dispose. MockHttpServer bounds its history to 256 by default, MockTransport has no capacity. A soak run of one million 1 KB requests retains about 1 GB.

## Location
- `Runtime/Testing/MockTransport.cs:290`

## Problem
CaptureRequest (MockTransport.cs:285-291) calls SnapshotRequest, which copies the buffered body with ToArray() and builds a new UHttpRequest (365-381), and enqueues it in `_capturedRequests` (line 23), which is only emptied by ClearCapturedRequests or Dispose. MockHttpServer bounds its history (historyCapacity, default 256, MockHttpServer.cs:340-345); MockTransport has no capacity.

**Failure scenario.** A soak or benchmark run of 1,000,000 requests with 1 KB bodies through one MockTransport retains ~1 GB of request snapshots; allocation gates measured through MockTransport also include one body copy plus a request object per send.

## Suggested fix
Add a capacity (ring buffer, default a few hundred) or an opt-out for request capture, and document that captured requests are retained.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] MockTransport has a capture capacity (default a few hundred, oldest dropped) and an opt-out for request capture
- [ ] Retention behaviour is documented
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Testing/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Testing] RecordReplayTransport request key hashes only the first and last 64 KB of large bodies under a 'sha256:' prefix and carries dead code
body:
## Summary
For bodies over the large-body threshold ComputeBodyHash hashes only the edge slices plus the length but labels the result sha256 or hmac-sha256. Two uploads differing only in the middle get the same key and replay returns responses in recording order. The code also has a never-false redactSensitiveQueryValues flag, two identical normalize wrappers, an unreachable null check, unused attributes and unused usings.

## Location
- `Runtime/Testing/RecordReplayTransport.Keys.cs:104`

## Problem
NormalizeUriForStorage (RecordReplayTransport.Keys.cs:104-107) and NormalizeUriForKey (109-112) are identical, both passing redactSensitiveQueryValues: true, so the parameter of NormalizeUri/NormalizeQuery (114, 138, 169) is never false. ComputeBodyHash (RecordReplayTransport.Utilities.cs:71-134) hashes only BodyEdgeSliceBytes from each end plus the length when bodyLength > LargeBodyThresholdBytes (102-118) but still emits the 'sha256:'/'hmac-sha256:' prefix (124); the check 'algorithm == null' at 94-99 cannot be true after new HMACSHA256/SHA256.Create. The DTOs carry [Serializable] and auto-properties (RecordReplayTransport.cs:980-1014) although they are converted to dictionaries by hand, and RecordReplayTransport.cs imports System.Collections, System.Reflection and System.Runtime.InteropServices without using them.

**Failure scenario.** Two recorded uploads of the same size that differ only between byte 64 KB and the last 64 KB get the same request key; replay then returns the responses in recording order regardless of which body is sent.

## Suggested fix
Remove the flag and one of the two wrappers, either hash the whole body or name the scheme honestly in the key (for example 'sha256-edges:'), and delete the unreachable null check, the attributes and the unused usings.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Large bodies are either hashed completely or the key prefix names the scheme honestly (for example sha256-edges)
- [ ] The dead flag, duplicate wrapper, unreachable check, [Serializable] attributes and unused usings are removed
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Testing/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Testing] RecordReplay body redaction ignores Content-Encoding: gzip/deflate bodies are recorded as '[REDACTED]' and cannot be replayed
body:
## Summary
RecordReplayTransport sits below DecompressionInterceptor and so records still-compressed bytes with Content-Type: application/json. RedactJsonBody cannot parse them and stores the 10-byte placeholder, while Content-Encoding: gzip and the original Content-Length stay. Replay then fails to inflate the placeholder and the test gets a decompression UHttpException. Rewritten JSON bodies also leave Content-Length and ETag stale.

## Location
- `Runtime/Testing/RecordReplayTransport.Redaction.cs:81`

## Problem
RedactBodyIfNeeded classifies by Content-Type only (81-95, ClassifyBody 98-117). The transport sits below DecompressionInterceptor (Documentation~/Modules/Interceptors.md order #7), which adds 'Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate' (DecompressionInterceptor.cs:68-71), so RecordingHandler receives the still-compressed bytes with Content-Type: application/json and Content-Encoding: gzip. RedactJsonBody (119-132) fails to parse them and returns RedactUnparseableBody, i.e. the 10 bytes '[REDACTED]'; the only signal is Log(), and RecordReplayTransportOptions.Logger is null by default (RecordReplayTransport.cs:191, 726-729). The stored response headers keep Content-Encoding: gzip and the original Content-Length. Also when redaction does rewrite a JSON body (143) the stored Content-Length/ETag are left stale. No test in Tests/Runtime/Testing mentions gzip or Content-Encoding.

**Failure scenario.** Record a JSON API with the canonical interceptor stack (DecompressionInterceptor present, server gzips). SaveRecordings succeeds. In Replay mode every such response is replayed as '[REDACTED]' with Content-Encoding: gzip, DecompressionHandler fails to inflate it and the test gets a decompression UHttpException instead of the recorded JSON.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 8.4

## Suggested fix
When Content-Encoding is present and not identity, decode gzip/deflate (bounded by MaxRecordBytes) before redaction and store the decoded body with Content-Encoding/Content-Length rewritten, or fail the recording loudly through MarkRecordingFailed instead of storing a placeholder; rewrite Content-Length whenever redaction changes the body.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] For Content-Encoding other than identity, gzip/deflate bodies are decoded (bounded by MaxRecordBytes) before redaction and stored with Content-Encoding and Content-Length rewritten, or the recording fails loudly through MarkRecordingFailed
- [ ] Content-Length is rewritten whenever redaction changes the body
- [ ] A gzip JSON response recorded and replayed through the canonical interceptor stack returns the original JSON
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Testing/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Testing] RecordReplayTransport stores the HMAC key beside an HMAC of the unredacted request body, so redacted secrets can be guessed offline
body:
## Summary
RecordReplayTransport hashes the raw request body with a per-recording salt and writes both the digest and the salt into the recording file. The salt only defeats precomputed tables, so anyone holding the file can dictionary-attack a redacted low-entropy value such as a password. The code comment claims the opposite. Anyone who commits or shares recordings is affected.

## Location
- `Runtime/Testing/RecordReplayTransport.Utilities.cs:69`

## Problem
RecordInteraction computes requestHash = ComputeBodyHash(requestBody, _keySalt) over the raw body (RecordReplayTransport.cs:643-646) and stores it as RequestBodyHash and inside RequestKey next to the redacted body (663-673). SaveRecordings writes the HMAC key itself into the same file (KeySalt, RecordReplayTransport.cs:439). The comment at Utilities.cs:69-70 claims 'with one it is HMAC-SHA256, so a low-entropy body (a form with a password) cannot be guessed from it', which is wrong for a key published beside the digest: the salt only defeats precomputed tables. The same holds for ComputeKeyedValueHash of Authorization/Cookie values when the caller opts into matching them (Keys.cs:79-81). Tests only assert that the salt differs per recording (RecordReplayRedactionTests.cs:120-144).

**Failure scenario.** A recorded login 'username=alice&password=hunter2' is stored as 'username=alice&password=%5BREDACTED%5D' plus hmac-sha256(salt, original body) and the salt. Anyone with the committed recording reconstructs the body with a candidate password, HMACs it with the stored salt and compares: a dictionary attack at raw SHA-256 speed recovers the test account's password, which the redaction was meant to remove.

## Suggested fix
Hash the redacted form of the body on both sides (replay can apply the same redaction to the incoming request before hashing), so the digest carries no information about redacted values; for opted-in sensitive match headers document that the keyed hash is guessable for low-entropy values or key it with material that is not stored in the file. Fix the comment.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The request-body digest stored in a recording is computed over the redacted form of the body (replay applies the same redaction to the incoming request before hashing), so it carries no information about redacted values
- [ ] The keyed hash of opted-in Authorization/Cookie match values either uses key material not stored in the file or is documented as guessable for low-entropy values
- [ ] The misleading comment at RecordReplayTransport.Utilities.cs:69-70 is corrected
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit test under Tests/Runtime/Testing/ records a body with a known password, then fails if a hash computed from the stored salt and the candidate plaintext equals the stored digest

Verifier note: Traced. RecordInteraction hashes the raw (unredacted) buffered request body with _keySalt (RecordReplayTransport.cs:643-646), stores it as RequestBodyHash and inside RequestKey (663-670) beside the redacted body (654, 671-673); SaveRecordings writes the HMAC key into the same file (RecordReplayTransport.cs:439; Serialization.cs:27-28), and replay needs it there (605-607). So the comment at RecordReplayTransport.Utilities.cs:69-70 ('a low-entropy body (a form with a password) cannot be guessed from it') is wrong: the salt only prevents precomputation. Form redaction keeps every other byte as recorded (Redaction.cs:151-191), so the original body is reconstructible exactly with a candidate value and testable at HMAC-SHA256 speed. title: [Testing] RecordReplayTransport match keys ignore most of a large request body and all of a streaming one
body:
## Summary
ComputeBodyHash hashes only the first and last 64 KiB plus the length for bodies above 1 MiB, and streaming bodies such as FileRequestBody get the constant key 'sha256:empty'. Two uploads that differ in the middle or in file content produce identical keys. Under MismatchPolicy.Strict a regressed upload still matches the old recording and the test passes.

## Location
- `Runtime/Testing/RecordReplayTransport.Utilities.cs:102`

## Problem
ComputeBodyHash hashes only the first and last 64 KiB plus the length for bodies above 1 MiB (102-118). BuildRequestKey and RecordInteraction use the constant 'sha256:empty' whenever request.Content.TryGetBufferedData is false (RecordReplayTransport.Keys.cs:15-17, RecordReplayTransport.cs:643-646), which is the case for FileRequestBody and other streaming bodies; the recorded entry also stores no request body for them.

## Suggested fix
Hash the full body (incrementally) for buffered content, and for replayable streaming bodies hash a read session at record and replay time or mark the key as 'body not compared' and say so in the mismatch/log output and the documentation.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Buffered request bodies are hashed in full (incrementally) for the match key
- [ ] Replayable streaming bodies are hashed at record and replay time, or the key is explicitly marked 'body not compared' and that is shown in mismatch/log output and documented

title: [Testing] RecordReplay redacts URL query parameters by exact name only and logs the raw request URL
body:
## Summary
Query parameters are redacted by an exact-name set, while JSON and form fields use a matcher that ignores case and separators. Names such as accessToken, access-token, clientSecret or presigned X-Amz-Signature are stored verbatim in entry.Url and RequestKey. The user logger also prints the unredacted URI at line 560. Recordings and logs can leak credentials.

## Location
- `Runtime/Testing/RecordReplayTransport.cs:70`

## Problem
ShouldRedactQueryParameter is QueryParameterNames.Contains(queryKey) (70-73) against the list at 147-163; ShouldRedactJsonField/ShouldRedactFormField use MatchesNormalized (80-111), which ignores '_', '-', '.', spaces and case. NormalizeQuery (RecordReplayTransport.Keys.cs:169) uses the exact form for both the stored Url and the match key. Separately, line 560 logs '{request.Method} {request.Uri}' unredacted to the user logger.

**Failure scenario.** GET /v1/me?accessToken=SECRET, ?access-token=SECRET, ?clientSecret=.. or a presigned ?X-Amz-Signature=..&X-Amz-Security-Token=.. is stored verbatim in entry.Url and RequestKey, although the same names are redacted in a JSON or form body of the same request.

## Suggested fix
Use the normalized matcher for query names too, add the common signed-URL parameters (X-Amz-Signature, X-Amz-Security-Token, X-Amz-Credential, X-Goog-Signature) to the defaults, and pass NormalizeUriForStorage(request.Uri) to the log line.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Query parameter names are matched with the same normalized matcher as JSON and form fields
- [ ] Default redaction list includes X-Amz-Signature, X-Amz-Security-Token, X-Amz-Credential and X-Goog-Signature
- [ ] The log line at RecordReplayTransport.cs:560 uses NormalizeUriForStorage(request.Uri)
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit test under Tests/Runtime/Testing/ records requests with ?access-token=, ?clientSecret= and X-Amz-Signature and asserts the stored Url, RequestKey and log output contain no secret

title: [Testing] Redaction defaults are duplicated between Observability.RedactionPolicy and RecordReplayRedactionPolicy and already diverge
body:
## Summary
Both modules hold their own private copy of the same 13 sensitive header names and their own '[REDACTED]' constant, with different semantics for trimming, query values and body fields. Core has no shared primitive, so a name added to one list is missed by the other. The Monitor/Logging path and the recording path can then disagree about what is secret.

## Location
- `Runtime/Testing/RecordReplayTransport.cs:130`

## Problem
Runtime/Observability/RedactionPolicy.cs:23-38 and Runtime/Testing/RecordReplayTransport.cs:130-145 each hold the same 13 header names in a private array; both define their own "[REDACTED]" (RedactionPolicy.cs:21 const, RecordReplayTransport.cs:37 static readonly). Divergence: Observability is immutable, trims names (RedactionPolicy.cs:127), redacts every query value and URL user-info (158-181) and never touches bodies; Testing is mutable (39-42), does not trim (65-68), redacts only named query parameters (RecordReplayTransport.Keys.cs:169-172) and redacts JSON/form body fields (Redaction.cs:81-95). Core has no shared primitive (rg finds no redaction code in Runtime/Core), and modules may only reference Core.

**Failure scenario.** A new sensitive header or token field is added to one list only; the Monitor/Logging path and the recording path then disagree about what is a secret.

## Suggested fix
Covered by #117 (one policy object for every site); put the shared name tables and placeholder in Core so both modules consume them.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Shared sensitive-name tables and the placeholder live in Core and both modules consume them
- [ ] Adding a header name to the shared table redacts it in both Observability and RecordReplay
- [ ] Existing redaction behavior of each module is preserved except where the shared policy intentionally unifies it, documented in the PR

title: [Testing] RecordReplayTransport keeps the caller's mutable RecordReplayRedactionPolicy by reference and reads it from dispatch threads
body:
## Summary
The constructor stores options.RedactionPolicy as is, although its public HashSets and RedactedValue are mutable, while other option sets are copied. Dispatch threads read them unsynchronized, and RedactedValue = null makes Utf8.GetBytes and Uri.EscapeDataString throw. A fixture sharing one policy across transports can mutate a HashSet during concurrent reads.

## Location
- `Runtime/Testing/RecordReplayTransport.cs:294`

## Problem
RecordReplayRedactionPolicy exposes three public HashSet<string> properties and a settable RedactedValue (RecordReplayTransport.cs:39-42). The constructor stores options.RedactionPolicy as is (294), whereas it copies MatchHeaderNames into its own sets (297-323). Dispatch threads call HeaderNames.Contains, enumerate JsonBodyFieldNames (96-111) and read RedactedValue (Redaction.cs:27, 185, 198, 259) with no synchronization. RedactedValue = null makes Utf8.GetBytes(null) throw in RedactUnparseableBody (Redaction.cs:198) and Uri.EscapeDataString(null) throw in RedactFormBody (185). MatchesNormalized also builds a StringBuilder per configured name for every JSON key (103-108, 113-128).

**Failure scenario.** A fixture shares one policy across transports and adds a header name in a later test's setup while an earlier transport is still recording: HashSet is mutated during a concurrent Contains, or the earlier recording's redaction set changes halfway through.

## Suggested fix
Snapshot the policy into an immutable internal form in the constructor (pre-normalized name sets, non-null placeholder), matching the immutable Observability.RedactionPolicy.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The constructor snapshots the policy into an immutable internal form with pre-normalized name sets and a non-null placeholder
- [ ] Mutating the caller's policy after construction does not change an existing transport's redaction
- [ ] RedactedValue = null is rejected or replaced by the default instead of throwing during redaction

title: [Testing] RecordReplayTransport writes recordings that Replay cannot load because LiteJson rejects input above 16 MiB
body:
## Summary
Replay parses the whole recording through JsonSerializer.Default, which routes to LiteJsonSerializer with an immutable 16 MiB input limit. Record accepts up to 16 MB per response, stores bodies as base64 (4/3 inflation) and has no total bound. A session with one 13 MB download or twenty 1 MB responses saves successfully and then fails to load with InvalidOperationException in Replay mode.

## Location
- `Runtime/Testing/RecordReplayTransport.cs:593`

## Problem
LoadRecordings reads the file with File.ReadAllText and calls DeserializeJson(json, typeof(Dictionary<string, object>)) (RecordReplayTransport.cs:592-593), which goes through ProjectJsonBridge (RecordReplayTransport.Serialization.cs:271-282) to JsonSerializer.Default. Both stock defaults route that shape to LiteJsonSerializer.Instance (Runtime/Bootstrap/JsonUtilitySerializer.cs:245), whose immutable MaxInputBytes is 16 MiB (LiteJsonSerializer.cs:39, 150-155) -> JsonSerializationException wrapped as 'RecordReplay deserialization failed.'. On the record side MaxRecordBytes defaults to 16 MB per response (RecordReplayTransport.cs:200, 214), bodies are stored as base64 (4/3 inflation, 671-678) and SaveRecordings serialises all entries with no total limit (417-455). No test in Tests/Runtime/Testing exercises a recording near the cap.

**Failure scenario.** Record a session containing one 13 MB asset download (17.3 MB of base64) or twenty 1 MB responses: recording and SaveRecordings succeed ('recordings are never truncated'), and constructing the transport in Replay mode then always throws InvalidOperationException, so the fixture is unusable without registering another serializer.

## Suggested fix
Enforce one consistent bound: either fail SaveRecordings (or the offending request) when the serialised recording would exceed what Replay can load, or let Replay parse with a dedicated limit (a bridge entry point that takes a size cap, or per-entry files/streamed parsing) sized from MaxRecordBytes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Record fails (SaveRecordings or the offending request) when the serialised recording would exceed what Replay can load, or Replay parses with a limit sized from MaxRecordBytes
- [ ] A recording larger than 16 MiB either cannot be written with a clear error or loads successfully in Replay
- [ ] The behavior is documented in the module docs
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit test under Tests/Runtime/Testing/ records bodies totalling over 16 MiB and fails before the fix

title: [Testing] RecordReplayTransport keeps every recorded body as a base64 string in memory until SaveRecordings with no total bound
body:
## Summary
Record mode drains each body into several full-size copies, converts it to a base64 string and queues it unbounded until dispose. SaveRecordings then builds a dictionary tree and one JSON string for the whole file. Thirty 5 MB responses hold about 400 MB of strings, so long Editor sessions can run out of memory.

## Location
- `Runtime/Testing/RecordReplayTransport.cs:684`

## Problem
RecordingHandler drains a streamed body into a SegmentedBuffer, then `ToArray()`s it for the downstream handler (RecordReplayTransport.cs:840-843); RecordInteraction makes another array for redaction (RedactBodyIfNeeded -> ToExactByteArray, RecordReplayTransport.Redaction.cs:71-95) and converts it to a base64 string (671-678) that is enqueued in the unbounded `_recordedEntries` ConcurrentQueue (259, 684). SaveRecordings then builds a dictionary tree, one JSON string for the whole file and writes it with File.WriteAllText (431-453).

**Failure scenario.** Recording a play session with 30 responses of 5 MB: about 400 MB of base64 strings (2.67 bytes of heap per body byte) stay alive until dispose, each response transiently needs ~4 copies of its body, and the final save allocates the whole file again as one string; in the Editor this ends in an out-of-memory error for long sessions.

## Suggested fix
Bound the total recorded bytes (fail like the per-response limit), store bodies as byte[] until save, and write entries to the file incrementally instead of building one string.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Total recorded bytes are bounded and exceeding the bound fails like the per-response limit
- [ ] Bodies are held as byte[] until save
- [ ] SaveRecordings writes entries incrementally without building one string for the whole file
- [ ] Peak transient copies per recorded response are reduced to at most two, measured in a test

title: [Testing] RecordReplayTransport records a caller-cancelled request as a failed interaction when cancellation lands during body drain
body:
## Summary
When cancellation occurs while a streaming body is drained, the HandlerCallbackSafetyWrapper converts it into an UHttpException(Unknown) delivered to RecordingHandler.OnResponseError, which unconditionally records it with ThrowsException true. The cancellation branch that records nothing is only reached before the response head. A later identical request in Replay then gets an Unknown error instead of the recorded success.

## Location
- `Runtime/Testing/RecordReplayTransport.cs:818`

## Problem
RecordingHandler.OnResponseStartAsync drains a streaming body with the caller token and rethrows OperationCanceledException (808-823). The inner transport calls it through HandlerCallbackSafetyWrapper (RawSocketTransport.cs:1878-1893), whose AwaitResponseStartAsync catches every exception and calls ReportFailure -> _inner.OnResponseError(UHttpException(Unknown, 'The operation was canceled.', oce)) (HandlerCallbackSafetyWrapper.cs:83-128). That lands in RecordingHandler.OnResponseError (876-897), which unconditionally calls RecordInteraction(..., threwException: true). DispatchRecordAsync's OperationCanceledException branch (514-518), which records nothing, is only reached when the cancellation happens before the response head.

**Failure scenario.** A recorded session cancels a download mid-body (user navigates away) and then repeats the same request. The file holds two entries for the key: {StatusCode 200, Error Unknown 'The operation was canceled.', ThrowsException true} and the success. In Replay the first identical request gets an Unknown error instead of the recorded response.

## Suggested fix
In RecordingHandler.OnResponseError (and the UHttpException/Exception catch arms) skip RecordInteraction when the error is or wraps an OperationCanceledException with the caller token cancelled (the same test Core's CancellationClassification.TryGetCallerCancellation applies), and add a test that cancels during the drain.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] RecordingHandler skips RecordInteraction when the error is or wraps an OperationCanceledException with the caller token cancelled
- [ ] A request cancelled mid-body leaves no entry in the recording
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit test under Tests/Runtime/Testing/ cancels during the drain and asserts no interaction is recorded; it fails before the fix

## Problem
TurboHTTP.Testing.asmdef:5-11 has includePlatforms [], excludePlatforms [], defineConstraints [] (only autoReferenced:false), the same shape closed issue #196 described for BouncyCastle ("its DLL is part of every player build's linker input"). Runtime/TurboHTTP.Complete.asmdef:16 lists TurboHTTP.Testing although nothing in Runtime/Bootstrap uses a Testing type and asmdef references are not transitive (Tests/Editor/ModuleAutoReferenceTests.cs:10-13 says so). Editor/TurboHttpLinkerProcessor.cs:146-150 merges a module's link.xml whenever the owning DLL exists in the linker input, so Runtime/Testing/link.xml:7-16 (preserve=all for SHA256, SHA256Managed, HMACSHA256, RNGCryptoServiceProvider, SHA256CryptoServiceProvider) is applied to every build. The assembly is 2,973 lines (RecordReplayTransport 1,954 across 5 files, MockHttpServer 623, MockTransport 397) and pulls System.Text.RegularExpressions (MockHttpServer.cs:8,20-22,428-436, a process-wide static Regex cache), System.Linq and HMAC. Both Testing and Files also declare noEngineReferences:false without using UnityEngine (rg finds no UnityEngine use in Runtime/Testing or Runtime/Files), so nothing enforces that they stay engine-free.

**Failure scenario.** A shipping player built with Managed Stripping Disabled (Mono) or Minimal (IL2CPP, where user assemblies are copied unstripped) contains TurboHTTP.Testing.dll in full, including the Regex-based router and record/replay file writer; at any level the Testing link.xml crypto preserves are merged even though the project never uses the module. Whether Low/Medium/High drop the unreferenced assembly is unproven (same open question as #258).

## Suggested fix
Give the Testing asmdef a define constraint (UNITY_INCLUDE_TESTS || an explicit TURBOHTTP_TESTING opt-in), remove it from TurboHTTP.Complete's references, and set noEngineReferences:true on Testing and Files. Confirm with the #100 player-build smoke that the DLL is absent from ManagedStripped.
